We then forced the conceptual semi-distributed hydrological model COSERO with the 1 km2 gridded meteorological INCA product, which are both operationally used for hydropower and flood forecasting, and modeled thirteen high-alpine catchments in Austria between 2016 and 2024 at 500 m spatial and hourly temporal resolution. The assimilation of Sentinel-1 snow depths substantially improved overall model performance relative to modeling with uncorrected INCA data. For the entire 2016–2024 modeling period, this improvement is indicated by a median increase in NSE by 9.9% (0.75 to 0.82) and KGE by 34.1% (0.62 to 0.83), and a reduction in the median runoff deficit from −23.1% to −3.9%. The data assimilation in the operational modeling setup proved more effective during snow-poor years, a finding that may become more relevant under an increasingly warming climate in the European Alps. The Sentinel-1 snow depth product showed good agreement with ground measurements and snow cover maps (MODIS). Its assimilation remedied the winter precipitation deficit in INCA, while improving spatiotemporal snowpack simulation and enhancing snowmelt runoff prediction. This more realistic representation of the mountainous snowpack may benefit simulation of other hydrological variables including evapotranspiration, soil moisture, and groundwater recharge. The approach also shows promise for modeling remote, ungauged basins globally. These results demonstrate the value of integrating satellite-derived snow information for operational alpine hydrological modeling and water resource assessment.

title: Spatiotemporal hydrological connectivity on karst hillslopes: Insights from high-frequency moisture monitoring
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Yutong Zhang, Jun Zhang, Fa Wang, Jinjiao Lian, Zhiyong Fu, Hongsong Chen
abstract: Hydrological connectivity (HC) crucially controls runoff generation and biogeochemical transport in terrestrial ecosystems. However, how subsurface structural heterogeneity regulates HC in complex karst environments remains poorly understood. The modulating role of soil thickness on HC dynamics was investigated using high-frequency (5-min) soil moisture monitoring across two karst hillslopes with contrasting mean soil depth (35 cm vs. 66 cm). HC was identified by soil saturation conditions, while its spatiotemporal characteristics were quantified using metrics including connectivity strength (CS), response timing (Ts), and peak lag time (Tp). Results showed that both hillslopes followed a downslope-to-upslope expansion sequence consistent with the “fill-and-spill” mechanism, but their tempo differed fundamentally. The shallow-soil hillslope (SSP) exhibited higher CS (mean 0.39 vs. 0.35) and faster connectivity initiation (6.30 h) than the deep-soil hillslope (DSP, 7.45 h). Analysis of vertical lag times revealed a more pronounced expression of rapid-recharge preferential flow (negative lags) within the SSP, whereas the DSP maintained stronger matrix resistance and buffering capacity. Distinct, soil-thickness-dependent nonlinear rainfall thresholds for HC activation were identified (46.4 mm for SSP vs. 53.0 mm for DSP). Beyond these thresholds, CS on the DSP followed a predictable, rainfall-controlled linear trajectory; in contrast, the SSP exhibited heightened sensitivity to antecedent soil moisture, driven by the complex coupling between bedrock micro-topography and soil thickness variations. These findings suggest that hydrological models in karst regions should incorporate the high spatial variability of soil thickness, rather than relying on average values, to better predict hillslope-scale runoff generation.

title: Geometric controls on heterogeneous recession and vulnerability of glaciers in the Mount Everest region, central Himalaya
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Yanlong Zhao, Tanguang Gao, Wanqin Guo, Jiansheng Feng, Shuochen Qin, Shichang Kang
abstract: The physical mechanisms governing the heterogeneous recession of central Himalayan glaciers remain debated, particularly regarding the competing roles of geometric versus surface controls. While traditional coarse-resolution studies often emphasize the regulating effects of debris and lakes, their dominance at the regional scale has not been rigorously quantified, creating uncertainty in catchment-scale runoff projections. Here, we conducted a comprehensive assessment of glacier change and vulnerability based on high-resolution ZY-3 imagery from 2012 to 2021. We established a high-precision glacier inventory and developed a multi-dimensional vulnerability index through a hybrid AHP-Random Forest approach. We find that the spatial heterogeneity is overwhelmingly determined by geometric controls. Topographic and morphological factors collectively account for 98.03% (95% CI: 96.31%–99.16%) of the total relative contribution, whereas surface-condition variables contribute only 1.97% (95% CI: 0.84%–3.69%), with altitude, slope, length-to-width ratio, and glacier area jointly contributing over 60% of the total. Governed by these geometric constraints, 32.6% of the region’s glaciers have suffered a complete loss of accumulation area, transitioning into a state of progressive decay independent of short-term climate variability, signaling a weakening of the drought-buffering capacity in headwater catchments. Furthermore, the vulnerability assessment highlights a profound structural imbalance between total area and glacier count. While the few large glaciers dominating the total area are moderately vulnerable, 81.5% of individual glaciers are systematically classified as having High to Very High vulnerability due to unfavorable geometric configurations. This study demonstrates that glacier geometry, rather than surface conditions, is the principal driver of heterogeneous responses and future risk, offering critical insights for glacier and hydrological modeling and water resource management.

title: Pre-monsoon flow-path switching regulates downstream dissolved organic carbon dynamics in a high-alpine river on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Dong Zhang, Yindong Tong, Xiaodong Li, Yanli Sun, Jiajun Han
abstract: High-altitude semi-arid rivers undergo rapid hydrological reorganization during the pre-monsoon season, yet the respective roles of antecedent warming, initial thaw, and changes in hydrological connectivity in regulating the downstream export of dissolved organic carbon remain poorly understood. To clarify these controls, we conducted high-frequency monitoring at 3-day intervals in the Lhasa River Basin on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau from March to early July 2024. Dissolved organic carbon (DOC), dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), major ions, and stable isotopes (δ13C-DOC, δ13C-DIC, δD, and δ18O) were measured to trace water sources and carbon dynamics. Our results reveal a pronounced pre-monsoon hydrochemical turning point, driven primarily by seasonal flow-path switching rather than by direct glacier meltwater inputs. During the early pre-monsoon period (March–mid-May), river discharge was dominated by groundwater, and DIC and major ions increased gradually while DOC remained relatively low. Distinct hydrochemical and isotopic shifts occurred around mid-May, coinciding more closely with sharp increases in air temperature. After mid-May, the river transitioned to a more mixed hydrological regime, as indicated by marked shifts in water isotopes (δ18O: −17.0‰ to −14.5‰; d-excess: 9.3‰ to 13.5‰), declining DIC and major ion concentrations, increasing DOC concentrations (0.7–2.0 mg C·L−1), and progressively more depleted δ13C-DOC (−25.8‰ to −28.5‰) and δ13C-DIC values (−4.5‰ to −6.9‰). These coupled patterns suggest that antecedent warming and initial thaw preconditioned near-surface hydrological connectivity and reorganized flow paths, thereby increasing the DOC mobilization from shallow organic-rich source areas while diluting groundwater-derived DIC and major ions with low-solute near-surface waters, including thaw and snowmelt contributions. Comparisons with glacier-fed streams further indicate that glacier meltwater contributes only marginally to downstream DOC in the Lhasa River. Overall, our findings show that pre-monsoon carbon dynamics in this high-alpine river are controlled primarily by thermally driven hydrological switching superimposed on early-season thaw, highlighting the sensitivity of alpine carbon export to short-lived connectivity pulses on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.

title: Flood depth mapping with SWOT-derived training data: evaluating the potential of open-source datasets
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Zixi Li, Jiayin Xiao, Fuqiang Tian, Fuxin Chai
abstract: Flood depth is a critical parameter for disaster relief and damage assessment, yet pixel-level ground-truth data remain scarce. Traditional approaches, including digital elevation model (DEM) based methods and hydrodynamic simulations, are constrained by data accuracy, cost, and limited generalization. This study proposes machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) frameworks for flood depth estimation using only open-source datasets. Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite observations were used to construct a pixel-level flood depth reference dataset for model training. Multi-channel inputs include DEM, slope, aspect, SAR/optical-derived flood extent, and AlphaEarth data, with channel- and self- attention mechanisms enhancing feature representation. Results from two test datasets show that both ML and DL outperform the baselines. Ablation experiments further confirm the value of attention mechanisms and Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) in handling high-dimensional features. Validation with in situ measurements from the Haihe River Basin indicates that different flood extent extraction methods affect results, though differences are not statistically significant. The DL framework further demonstrates improved robustness to DEM uncertainties, reducing RMSE by 10–50 % across three test datasets. Overall, the results highlight the potential of combining SWOT with open-source data for flood depth mapping, while noting limitations related to SWOT event availability and DEM accuracy.

title: Possibility of SWE estimation from snow cover extent using the dynamic non-Gaussian snow depletion curve
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Noriaki Ohara, Rui A.P. Perdigão
abstract: Seasonal snow cover in mountainous regions has been regularly monitored by ground-based snow surveys and remote sensing techniques to serve as a predictor of water availability during the upcoming spring season in downstream regions. The objective of this study is to estimate the snow water equivalent (SWE) from the observable snow cover fraction (SCF) using the Pires & Perdigão (2007) non-Gaussian multivariate information-theoretic metric. This metric articulates higher-order cross-cumulants and Hermite polynomials into Edgeworth expansions to yield an analytical approximation of the conditional expectation (snow depletion curve, SDC) as well as the joint probability density functions (PDFs). The predictability of SWE from SCF was diagnosed by mutual information (MI) using 110 high-resolution snow distribution data from the NASA Airborne Snow Observatory (ASO). The results suggest that the non-Gaussian component can improve the estimation of SWE in addition to the regular Gaussian correlation method, while the MI generally decreases as the SCF approaches 1 (complete snow cover). Additionally, based on the distributed snow model, the possibility of higher-order statistical cumulant estimation was examined in the Upper Tuolumne River watershed. This analysis demonstrated that the non-Gaussian (non-linear) information metric can potentially provide the basin total SWE using estimated cross-cumulants from the marginal PDF of the remotely observed SCF.

title: Evolution and mechanisms of tidal duration asymmetry in the Xijiang River Channel of the Pearl River Estuary
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Xianzhao He, Shuai Hu, Xiangyuan Li, Haichen Liu, Min Gao, Jianliang Lin, Xiaohe Zhang, Lixia Niu, Qingshu Yang
abstract: Tidal Duration Asymmetry (TDA), defined as the inequality between flood- and ebb-tide durations, affects water resource security and material transport. This study investigates the evolution and underlying mechanisms of TDA in the Xijiang River Channel of the Pearl River Estuary using observed water levels (1966–2016) and Delft3D-FM hydrodynamic modeling. TDA shows spring-neap variations, seasonal fluctuations, and stepwise alterations. For the spring-neap variations, an increase in tidal range shifts downstream TDA toward ebb dominance (shorter ebb duration), while the effect upstream is minor. Seasonal variations in TDA are closely linked to river discharge and exhibit clear threshold behavior. When discharge remains below a critical range (1.1 × 104 –1.6 × 104 m3/s), increasing discharge enhances flood dominance (shorter flood duration), whereas discharge exceeding this range promotes ebb dominance. Stepwise alterations in TDA toward ebb dominance have occurred in the Xijiang River Channel, which are associated with increases in M2 amplitudes induced by extensive shoreline reclamation. These results highlight the vital role of river-tide interaction and topographic changes in reshaping estuarine tidal asymmetry, providing theoretical insights for adaptive water resource management and estuarine engineering, particularly for saltwater intrusion control and sediment management.

title: On the storm direction and peak floods in the continental United States, 1950–2024
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Mochi Liao
abstract: Storm direction has significant impacts on land surfaces, such as flood responses and soil erosion. With projected increases (e.g., frequency and magnitude) in extreme precipitation events across many regions of the world, it is worthwhile to explore possible changes in storm characteristics, especially as more data have become available during the satellite era over the past three decades. In this study, we focus on understanding and characterizing storm directions over the continental United States (CONUS). Specifically, a new storm direction model is developed and applied to model-based reanalysis (ERA5L, 9 km resolution) and surface measurement-based reanalysis (AORC, 4 km resolution). This study shows strong variability in storm directions over the Great Plains and spatial patterns of storm preferential direction (based on frequency) related to topography and climate regimes across CONUS. This study also reveals differences in storm travel distance and storm duration at event scales, conditional on whether the storm comes from a preferential or non-preferential direction. For example, the median storm travel distance is increased by 35 km when storms come from the preferential direction. Flood peaks are higher by a median of 50–100% when stream directions align with storm directions for mid-sized basins (1500 km2 to 2500 km2). Furthermore, the spacetime trajectory of maximum precipitation rate (referred to as Potential Peak Precipitation or PPP) derived from the new storm direction approach provides an integrated picture of storm dynamics, and AORC-based PPP is shown to be on the equivalent magnitude of observed maximum precipitation at event scales, particularly along the southern and southeastern coasts.

title: Reconstruction and evolution analysis of long-term terrestrial water storage anomalies in Xinjiang based on time series decomposition and multi-model coupling
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Zilong Li, Zhenxia Mu, Jing Liu, Xiaoyan Qiu
abstract: The Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and its successor GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) provide a new observational method for monitoring large-scale Terrestrial Water Storage Anomalies (TWSA). However, existing TWSA records cover only the period since 2002 and exhibit mission discontinuities, which limits their applicability in studies of long-term hydrological changes. Therefore, this study proposes a TWSA component reconstruction framework coupled with time-series decomposition, the VIC hydrological model and machine learning to reconstruct a monthly-scale TWSA dataset at a resolution of 0.25°×0.25° from 1961 to 2022 in Xinjiang, and to verify its reliability using JPL and CSR Mascon products and multi-source observation data. The main findings of this study include: (1) During the GRACE observation period, the reconstructed TWSA exhibits high consistency with CSR-Mascon and JPL-Mascon in spatiotemporal distributions: approximately 70% of grids have CC > 0.6, over 60% have NSE > 0.6, and more than 80% of grid cells have RMSE 0.60) with CNRD v1.0 and TerraClimate runoff depth in 57% and 85% of the areas, respectively, with local CCs exceeding 0.85, indicating that the reconstructed TWSA can reasonably reflect the hydrological response characteristics of runoff variations. (3) Reconstruction results show that the TWSA in Xinjiang exhibited a predominantly downward trend from 1961 to 2022, with 60.8% of the study area showing a downward trend. The intra-annual variation shows a surplus in winter and deficits in spring and summer, and the seasonal amplitude and long-term trend exhibit significant spatial heterogeneity. The reconstructed long-term TWSA dataset provides a data foundation for diagnosing water storage evolution, monitoring hydrological droughts, and assessing water resources in Xinjiang.

title: Coupling ORCHESTRA with HYDRUS to simulate multicomponent reactive transport in variably saturated porous media
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): J.A.R. Soedarso, D.W.S. Tang, G. Sigmund, N.B. Sutton, H.H.M. Rijnaarts, J.C.L. Meeussen
abstract: We develop and demonstrate the coupling of the variably saturated flow and transport model HYDRUS-1D, with the geochemical reaction model ORCHESTRA, for simulating multicomponent reactive transport in soils and other porous media. We implement a loose coupling of HYDRUS and ORCHESTRA that feeds flow information simulated by HYDRUS into ORCHESTRA, where arbitrary multicomponent reactions, transformations, and kinetics can be implemented. The HYDRUS-ORCHESTRA coupled model is evaluated with four test cases of increasing complexity in a 100-cell, 1-meter deep unsaturated zone, including transient flow conditions and active internal sinks (root water and solute uptake). The aim was to examine the accuracy of the coupled model against HYDRUS, which can simulate simple reactive transport scenarios. The coupled model is accurate, with <0.65% deviation in outflow breakthrough times, and ∼1% deviation in terminal solute mass balances compared to HYDRUS. The coupled model’s agreement with HYDRUS increases with transport distance and grid refinement, because the deviations stem from numerical dispersion. This novel methodology makes it possible to simulate the fate of arbitrary reactive substances, nutrients, energy, and isotopes under transient, variably saturated conditions including plant-soil–water interactions. Such flexibility is particularly crucial for emerging contaminants, which can exhibit diverse novel and complex reactive behaviours.

title: Three Gorges Reservoir operations regulate nitrogen transport and transformation via hydrology-sediment-carbon interactions
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Bei Nie, Yu Bai, Wei Zha, Shan Zhang, Miaomiao Chen
abstract: The global proliferation of reservoir construction has fundamentally altered nitrogen cycling across spatiotemporal scales. However, uncertainties persist regarding natural and anthropogenic regulation impacts on nitrogen transport-transformation processes in the reservoir, limiting the knowledge of accurately predicting different nitrogen components. Incorporating characteristics of sediment-mediated and drying-wetting process in the Three Gorges Reservoir (TGR), this study developed a novel Hydro-Sediment-Biogeochemical Model (HSBM) to systematically evaluate synergistic effects of reservoir operational schemes, sediment fluxes, and carbon inputs on nitrogen transport and transformation. The HSBM revealed that nitrogen dynamics in the TGR were engineered by three key drivers: reservoir operation, sediment load, and carbon input. Specifically, reservoir operation drove decreases in NH4 +-N and NO3 −-N concentrations that were inversely correlated with water level and impoundment duration, while nitrogen emissions scaled linearly with the drying-rewetting coefficient Kz , showing the strongest regulation during frequent fluctuating periods. Increased sediment loads suppressed nitrogen concentrations in water column while exponentially enhancing nitrogen emissions, with peak corresponding to low-water-level season. Similar to sediment load, regulation of carbon input on nitrogen transformation was stronger, especially with a linear growth relationship between the carbon augmentation coefficient (Kax) and nitrogen emissions (2–18% increase per Kax unit). Mechanistically, these dynamics are collectively regulated by reservoir-mediated nitrogen cycling, specifically via expansion of drying-rewetting zones, sediment-associated adsorption and nitrification–denitrification coupling, and carbon-stimulated denitrification. These findings provide a process-based framework to support adaptive nitrogen management strategies in reservoir systems.

title: Wave damping ability of restored mangrove wetlands during typhoons: A case study from Hailing Island, China
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Zongyao Chen, Wen Wei, Yulu Yang, Xiufang Qiu, Zihao Deng, Peng He
abstract: As climate change intensifies coastal flooding, nature-based coastal defense is garnering global concern. Though mangrove restoration is being widely implemented, the protective capacity of restored mangroves against storm waves remains poorly quantified. In this study, a 13-day field observation of wave evolution and vegetation properties was conducted across a restored Kandelia obovata wetland on Hailing Island, China, during Typhoon Maliksi (2024), to investigate the storm wave damping performance of restored mangrove wetlands and their functionality as nature-based coastal defense. The results demonstrate an enhancement in wave height reduction by the restored mangrove wetland from normal to typhoon conditions, with a larger increase in bare flat (from 15% to 26%) than the mangrove zone (from 14% to 22%). Despite its small structural dimensions, the restored mangrove exhibited storm wave height reduction (39% across 100 m) comparable to that of Sonneratia sp. and Sonneratia apetala under similar wave conditions, and larger than that of Aegiceras corniculatum despite higher incident waves, as reported in previous studies. Furthermore, an idealized one-dimensional wave propagation model, incorporating vegetation drag and bed friction effects, was developed to explore the role of mangrove width in wave attenuation by the coupled bare flat-restored mangrove system. The model indicates that while wave attenuation increases with mangrove width, the marginal gain per-unit-width added diminishes as mangrove width increases. An optimal restoration width of 16% (of the total width) was then identified to balance protective effect and cost‑effectiveness, which is suitable for both normal and storm conditions but is largely site‑specific (depending on tidal regimes, geomorphic conditions, and vegetation properties). These findings underscore the critical role of restored mangrove wetlands in mitigating typhoon impacts and provide practical insights for designing effective nature-based coastal defenses.

title: A four-decade satellite record of coupled lake area and water quality responses to climate changes and human activities in Northwest China
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Ming Shen, Yuan Liu, Tianci Qi, Changjiang Liu, Zhigang Cao, Zhenyu Tan, Juhua Luo, Hongtao Duan
abstract: Understanding the coupled dynamics of lake (including natural lakes and reservoirs) water quantity and quality remains scarce, both regionally and globally. This study establishes a novel remote sensing–based framework to assess coupled lake quantity–quality dynamics, represented by lake area and Secchi disk depth (SDD), and to classify lakes into four ecological–hydrological trajectories (Types I–IV). Applying this framework to Landsat imagery (1986–2023) across 729 lakes (>1 km2) in Xinjiang, China. We found that lakes generally experienced area expansion and improved clarity (Sen’s slope > 0, p 0, p 0.1). Partial least squares regression (PLSR) revealed that temperature and cropland area were the primary drivers in northern and southern Xinjiang, reflecting the joint impacts of climate change and human water use and management. Conversely, precipitation and the Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) dominated in eastern Xinjiang, suggesting local hydroclimatic variability may offset the benefits of warming-induced glacier/snowmelt. This conceptual framework successfully links lake water quantity and quality, providing a scalable baseline for comprehensive lake assessments and sustainable water-resource management under climate change.

title: The global groundwater research knowledge divide
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Mahmood Sadat-Noori, Danial Khojasteh, Milad Haghani, Abbas Shamsipour, Martin S. Andersen
abstract: Groundwater underpins global water security, supporting nearly half of irrigation and domestic water use. Yet the scientific knowledge base informing its management is unevenly generated and disseminated. Here, we use large-scale bibliometric analysis of 53,163 groundwater-related scholarly publications produced over the last ∼50 years, combining keyword co-occurrence mapping, document co-citation analysis, and collaboration network analysis to examine the evolution of research themes, geographic contributions, and international collaboration networks. We show that groundwater science has expanded exponentially, shifting from predominantly local hydrogeological characterisation toward sustainability, water quality, and climate-resilience research. However, this growth is highly concentrated, as a small group of high-income countries accounts for 62% of publications and 68% of citations, while many groundwater-dependent regions remain marginal in both knowledge production and collaborative networks. These structural imbalances constrain the transfer of scientific insights to regions facing the greatest groundwater stress, risking maladaptive management and undermining progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 6, one of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals adopted by the United Nations. This study provides one of the most comprehensive global bibliometric assessments of groundwater research, quantifying thematic evolution, geographic inequities, and collaboration structures across the field. Our findings provide a quantitative foundation for rethinking how groundwater knowledge is generated and shared, highlighting the need for targeted capacity building, open data infrastructures, and more inclusive international research partnerships to support evidence-based groundwater management and accelerate progress toward SDG 6. Overall, the results highlight the urgency of prioritising equitable groundwater research investments to close the global groundwater knowledge divide.

title: Delayed and asymmetric groundwater responses to meteorological forcing across Germany revealed by lagged mutual information
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Fangfei Cai, Funing Ma, Zhenxue Dai, Junjun Chen
abstract: Delayed groundwater responses to meteorological forcing complicate drought recovery assessment, seasonal forecasting, and groundwater-resource management. Yet controls on recharge-groundwater response lags and their dependence on wet versus dry antecedent states remain poorly resolved at national scales. Using 32 years of weekly records from 3207 monitoring wells across Germany, we apply a model-free information-theoretic framework to quantify seasonal lagged dependence between an effective recharge proxy and groundwater levels. We compute maximum mutual information, optimal recharge-groundwater lags, optimal effective recharge proxy thresholds, and the dry versus wet antecedent-state asymmetry ratio. Statistically significant lagged dependence was detected in 12,812 season-well combinations under surrogate testing. Median lags ranged from 6 weeks in spring to 11 weeks in autumn and winter. Optimal recharge-groundwater lags were strongly associated with vertical stratification and aquifer architecture, increasing from 7 weeks in shallow systems ( 100 m), and from 5 weeks in karstic and fractured systems to 13 weeks in porous-and-fractured aquifers. Median state-dependent asymmetry did not differ significantly among aquifer media, while extreme dry-state dominance was spatially concentrated in fractured and karstic systems. Wet-state information dominated nationally with a median ratio of 0.565, whereas dry-state dominance became prominent in winter with a median ratio of 1.015. About 4% of records in summer and autumn were driven exclusively by drought precursors. These results identify hydrogeological controls on delayed groundwater responses and aquifer architectures vulnerable to moisture deficits, supporting seasonal forecasting and adaptive groundwater management.

title: Mechanism-guided dynamic machine learning overcomes environmental non-stationarity in algal bloom prediction
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Shujie Xu, Wenyu Zhang, Yong Tian, Shu-Chien Hsu, Chunmiao Zheng
abstract: Algal bloom prediction under environmental non-stationarity remains challenging, as historical regulatory thresholds frequently fail due to ecological concept drift. This study developed an integrated framework for Hong Kong rivers utilizing Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and Multiple Regression Trees (MRT) to extract complex structural associations and historical tipping points. However, rigorous generalization testing revealed threshold deactivation. Static MRT-guided discretization models collapsed (recall score = 0.32, ROC_AUC = 0.50) because long-term pollution baseline reductions drove phytoplankton adaptation. Permutation feature importance confirmed a mechanistic paradigm shift, transitioning from historical phosphorus constraints to complex nitrogenous limitations. To overcome this drift, we propose a novel dual-stage decision-support framework. While MRT is retained to establish interpretable, long-term policy baselines, continuous-variable Machine Learning is deployed to process the full environmental context, achieving highly adaptive, dynamic operational forecasting (recall score = 0.68, ROC_AUC = 0.89). Ultimately, this framework mitigates high-dimensional blind spots, providing a resilient blueprint for proactive watershed management under shifting ecological realities.

title: Characterizing spatiotemporal drought dynamics in the Yangtze River Basin: from event lifecycle to shifting climate drivers
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Ruiyang Hu, Ziyan Shi, Shanshui Yuan
abstract: The Yangtze River Basin is a critical agricultural and economic zone in China, where drought significantly impacts socioeconomic development. With the intensification of global warming, droughts in the Yangtze River Basin are expected to become more severe and frequent. However, the spatiotemporal dynamics of these droughts and the relative impacts of changing water supply (precipitation) and demand (evapotranspiration) remain poorly quantified. This study analyzes the spatiotemporal characteristics of meteorological drought events in the Yangtze River Basin using a three-dimensional clustering algorithm and examines the influence of climatic factors on the occurrence and development of droughts. Our results show a clear trend since the 21st century towards longer duration, larger area, and higher severity droughts, which are increasingly concentrated in the central basin. While PRE trends still dominate drought changes in 56% of the YRB under the PET formulation adopted, rising evaporative demand has increasingly influenced over the remaining 44%, indicating a shift in regional hydroclimate drivers.

title: Exogenous dust-induced snow albedo reduction and radiative forcing over the Third Pole
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Liang Li, Keqin Duan, Ting Yang, Yuhan Qi, Rong Chen, Peihong Shi
abstract: The evolution of snow over the Third Pole (TP) plays a critical role in amplifying changes in the Asian water tower. However, the quantitative contributions of exogenous dust to snow albedo reduction and radiative forcing over the TP remain largely unknown. Here, based on multi-source observations and numerical simulations of snow-darkening dynamic processes, this study systematically reveals the pronounced synchronicity and inverse coupling characteristics between dust and albedo changes over the TP, and quantifies the contributions of different exogenous dust to TP snow albedo reduction and radiative forcing. The results showed that exogenous dust-induced snow albedo reduction exhibited significant spatial heterogeneity, with core reduction regions concentrated in the northeastern TP and the southwestern slopes, where the regional mean albedo decrease exceeded 0.03 and locally surpassed 0.10. The dominant roles of different dust sources in snow darkening displayed significant spatiotemporal variability: dust from East Asia mainly affected regions below 3 km elevation of the north TP; dust from southwestern Asia and North Africa contributed 68.9% ± 22.2% and 20.9% ± 20.4%, respectively, to snow darkening in the central-western Himalayas, jointly dominating the snow darkening process in this region; whereas snow albedo reduction in the Pamir region was primarily influenced by dust from southwestern Asia and Central Asia, with Central Asian dust slightly prevailing during July–August. Exogenous dust deposition significantly enhanced the absorption of solar radiation by snow, generating total snow radiative forcing that generally exceeded 10 W m⁻2 in the major ice-snow covered regions. Among these effects, exogenous dust regulated the snow surface renewal process by altering snowfall frequency and snowfall amount, and the radiative forcing corresponding to this indirect regulatory pathway ranged from −7.6 to −1.3 W m⁻2. Meanwhile, exogenous dust also affected surface downward radiative fluxes by altering cloud-phase distribution, producing cloud-phase-related radiative forcing of approximately 0.3–0.69 W m⁻2. This study provides new quantitative perspectives and references for understanding the impacts of exogenous dust on the snow energy balance and hydrological processes over the TP.

title: Divergent 3D dynamics of subsurface lateral preferential flow network in broadleaf versus coniferous hillslopes: insights from time-lapse GPR
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Yun Hu, Hang Xu, Li Guo, Yi Jian, Jing Li, Feifei Hou, Xiaole Han, Jiancong Zhang, Genxu Wang
abstract: The mechanisms by which forest type modulates subsurface hydrologic connectivity and runoff generation remain poorly constrained, largely due to the difficulty of observing lateral preferential flow (LPF) dynamics in situ. This study integrated time-lapse ground-penetrating radar (GPR) with controlled infiltration experiments to quantitatively compare three-dimensional (3D) activation and evolution of subsurface LPF on adjacent broadleaf (BF) and coniferous (CF) forest hillslopes. Structural similarity (SSIM) index analysis was applied to GPR images collected across five parallel 1.5 m transects spaced at 0.3 m intervals, enabling mapping of spatiotemporal development of 3D LPF networks. Geophysical observations were independently supported by concurrent measurements of rainfall, soil moisture, and subsurface runoff in adjacent hillslopes. Our results reveal distinct, forest type-dependent LPF regimes: (1) On the BF hillslope, LPF activated rapidly and in a spatially connected manner, mainly at 0.6–1.0 m depth, likely along root channels and the soil-saprock interface. The volume of soil conducting LPF surged from 28.7% to 58.1% after the first infiltration pulse, then receded to 52.8% following the second. (2) In contrast, on the CF hillslope, activation was delayed and shallower, occurring mainly at depths of 0.2–0.4 m. Here, the activated soil volume for LPF increased incrementally from 14.1% to 32.4% after the first pulse and to 46.3% after the second. (3) Hydrometric measurements mirrored these geophysically derived 3D LPF patterns. BF showed higher soil-moisture response frequencies to rainfall input (0.776 vs 0.704) and larger amplitudes, consistent with more rapid and extensive LPF activation, together with sustained deeper subsurface runoff peaking at 4.18 mm at 0.6 m depth. In contrast, CF runoff was mainly shallow and attenuated, peaking at 3.56 mm at a depth of 0.1 m. Our findings demonstrate that, in addition to aboveground rainfall partitioning (effective water input), forest type regulates rainfall-runoff regimes by controlling subsurface Critical Zone connectivity. By quantifying these structure-process interactions, this study provides a transferable hydrogeophysical framework for advancing hillslope hydrological monitoring and offers new insights into vegetation’s regulation of subsurface runoff generation.

title: Effect of soil hysteresis on liquid-vapor-air flow in seasonally frozen soils
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Lianyu Yu, Huanjie Cai, Delan Zhu, Fubin Sun, Xiangxiang Ji, La Zhuo
abstract: Mass transfer in seasonally frozen ground is crucial for the frozen soil hydrology and ecohydrology processes and adaptive management. The increasingly frequent soil hysteresis phenomenon (SHP) makes it more complex. However, the influencing mechanism of soil hysteresis on the coupled liquid–vapor-air flow in the seasonally frozen soils is not yet fully understood. In this study, the STEMMUS-FT model (Simultaneous Transfer of Energy, Mass and Momentum in Unsaturated Soil with Freeze and Thaw) with the hysteresis effect was developed and verified against the field measurements of soil water content and temperature in a typical dry plateau. The dynamics of soil hydrothermal regimes were well simulated, with the values of RMSE lower than 0.95 °C and 0.02 m3 m−3 for the soil temperature and moisture simulations, respectively. Constrained by the prescribed boundary conditions, the hysteresis effect on the simulated temperature is negligible. There is a depth-dependent effect on the soil water content. Soil evaporation was overestimated during the unfrozen period when neglecting the hysteresis effect. The isothermal liquid flux, driven by the soil matric potential gradient, is the main reason for such overestimation. During the freezing period, soil ice was advanced with a higher value by considering the hysteresis effect. The effect of blocking and cryosuction on the mass transfer due to the presence of soil ice appeared to be enhanced. For the advective fluxes, the magnitude was dampened by the hysteresis except after precipitation during the freezing period. This study clarifies the influencing mechanisms of hysteresis on the liquid–vapor-air flow in the seasonally frozen soils and provides more insights for better portraying the frozen soil hydrological processes.

title: Incorporating variable source areas into rainfall-runoff pollutant export modeling for rural residential catchment
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Xuan Huang, Xu Yang, Yuhang Zhang, Man Lang, Ping Li, Kebing Chen, Dongli She, Yongqiu Xia
abstract: Rural non-point source pollution is primarily driven by rainfall runoff. The heterogeneous landscape of rural catchments, along with variable contributing source areas, result in complex pollutant export processes during rainfall events. Consequently, making accurate simulation of pollutant export during rainfall is both essential and challenging for effective water quality management. Existing Rainfall Runoff Model (RRM) assumes uniform contributing areas with exponential pollutant wash-off during rainfall, ignoring rural landscape complexity and dynamic expansion of contributing areas, leading to systematic errors during initial and peak rainfall periods. In this study, we propose a Modified Exponential Model (MEM) that integrates Variable Source Area (VSA) theory, using two parameters, α and β, which represent the maximum extent of VSA-contributing areas and their dynamic activation rates, respectively. The model was validated and applied to dissolved nitrogen (DN) and dissolved phosphorus (DP) modelling in rural residential catchments in the Yangtze River basin. We show that the MEM significantly outperformed RRM, particularly during medium and long-duration rainfall events (Regimes II and III), with Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) coefficients increasing by 0.15–0.24 for DN and 0.31–0.42 for DP. We also observed distinct parameter characteristics between pollutants: DN exhibited higher contributing area values (α: 0.076–0.924) than DP (α: 0.022–0.299). SHAP analysis demonstrated that runoff characteristics primarily modulate DN transport, while precipitation features more strongly influence DP dynamics. These findings not only deepen our understanding of rural pollutant export processes but also deliver a practical, interpretable modeling framework for water quality management in rural areas.

title: A revisit of slug injection in a finite-domain porous media: theory, experimental validation, and multi-parameter estimation
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Xiaosong Dong, Yanrong Zhao, Yong Huang, Jinguo Wang, Haonan Wang, Kehan Miao, Jie Zhang, Yuxing Zhang
abstract: Accurate prediction of solute transport in porous media is essential for groundwater remediation, and reliable parameter estimation is fundamental to tracer test interpretation. Classical infinite-domain advection–dispersion models are analytically convenient, but their idealized boundary conditions may be inadequate for finite domains. This study reformulates slug injection as a finite-reservoir boundary process rather than an idealized point source, linking inlet solute depletion, outlet constraint, and multi-parameter estimation within a finite-domain framework. This formulation avoids the near-source singularity inherent in the Dirac delta representation used in classical solutions. A Laplace-domain semi-analytical solution is derived and verified against numerical solution and the Sauty (1980) solution. Parametric analysis shows that the Péclet number governs advection–dispersion dominance, while the structural coefficient modulates peak concentrations. Sand-column experiments confirm that the finite-domain solution reproduces measured breakthrough curves more consistently than the Sauty solution. The framework enables simultaneous estimation of six parameters: hydraulic conductivity K , porosity n , pore velocity u , longitudinal dispersion coefficient D L , molecular diffusion coefficient D m , and longitudinal dispersivity α L . Estimated K and n are 1.67 × 10 - 3 m/s and 0.412, matching independent measurements; α L = 2.25 × 10 - 3 m and D m = 4.65 × 10 - 8 m2/s, with the D L – u regression yielding R 2 = 0.989 . These results demonstrate that explicitly accounting for finite-domain boundaries improves slug-injection interpretation and supports physically consistent multi-parameter identification.

title: Sequential estimation of aquifer parameters using water table elevations
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Ankush Kaundal, Sekhar Muddu
abstract: Groundwater level time series contain valuable information about aquifer storage properties and the external source–sink terms to which aquifer systems are subjected. However, estimating these source–sink terms from water table fluctuations remains challenging due to the difficulty of quantifying specific yield at the field scale and uncertainty associated with it. Strong correlations among recharge, pumping, and specific yield further complicate inference; without explicit uncertainty quantification, water table fluctuation-based models are prone to parameter non-uniqueness and substantial uncertainty propagation. Moreover, such models are commonly calibrated by estimating all parameters simultaneously, and the relative performance of simultaneous versus sequential parameter estimation for reliable parameter recovery has not been systematically investigated in such models. In this study, we develop an inverse modelling framework to quantify parameter uncertainty and correlation in water table fluctuation-based groundwater models and to assess whether sequential, iterative parameter estimation yields more reliable recovery of aquifer parameters than conventional simultaneous estimation. The methodology is first tested using synthetic water table fluctuations generated with known model parameters, enabling direct comparison between simultaneous and sequential estimation strategies. Simultaneous estimation exhibits strong equifinality and large errors, particularly in recharge and inferred pumping (up to 110%), whereas the sequential approach markedly improves parameter identifiability and recovers recharge, pumping, and specific yield with mean errors below 13%. The framework is subsequently applied to groundwater-level time series from 73 field borewells, demonstrating its ability to recover physically plausible aquifer parameters and groundwater forcings. The results further show that the framework can diagnose model structural errors, particularly those arising from neglecting groundwater abstraction when it is present. Leveraging millions of simulations executed using parallel processing, the approach efficiently addresses key uncertainties in water table fluctuation–based models and provides a practical means of inferring aquifer parameters and forcings directly from groundwater observations.

title: Diverging seasonal trends in soil moisture in Northern Europe
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Matthew L. Newell, Martin Drews, Morten Andreas Dahl Larsen, Mark R. Payne
abstract: The observed trends in wetness across Europe bear a clear imprint of climate change: for more than six decades, Northern Europe has become significantly wetter, while Southern and parts of Central Europe face growing aridity due to changes in annual precipitation patterns. These changing hydrological conditions have resulted in varying hydrological risks across different regions. While many studies have focused on drought in southern Europe, changes in seasonal and sub-seasonal soil moisture conditions in the north have received considerably less attention. In this paper, we examine seasonal and sub-seasonal patterns in average and extreme soil moisture conditions across Northern Europe, shedding light on emerging trends and changing hydrological conditions with the potential for high impacts regionally. The study analyzes soil moisture in Northern Europe using ERA5-Land data from 1961 to 2020. We apply the modified Mann-Kendall test to assess trends and compare two climatological periods (1961–1990 and 1991–2020). Our findings show an increase in the number of soil moisture surplus days (SMSD) by 9.9 days and consecutive soil moisture surplus days (CSMSD) by 5.3 days in southern Norway and central Sweden. In spring, the number of soil moisture deficit days (SMDD) increased by 6.3 days and consecutive soil moisture deficit days (CSMDD) by 6.1 days in southern areas of Northern Europe. Without interventions, rapid winter-spring seasonal transitions in soil moisture, particularly in southern Sweden and the Baltic region, could increasingly challenge land use and water management both in the present and future.

title: A novel high-resolution downscaling method for daily extreme precipitation using Sentinel-5P cloud parameters
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Yuting Luo, Hongwei Zeng, Junbin Li, Yang Chen, Jiangyuan Zeng, Miao Zhang, Hantian Wu, Lu Sun, Bingfang Wu
abstract: Statistical downscaling of daily extreme precipitation remains challenging due to the limited availability of optical observations during rainfall events, delayed vegetation responses to precipitation, and the coarse resolution of soil moisture and reanalysis-based predictors. To address these limitations, this study proposed a cloud variable based DeepGeo Downscaler (DGD) framework for daily extreme precipitation downscaling. The DGD used daily cloud physical parameters derived from Sentinel-5P as physically meaningful and near real time predictors and employed a hybrid of convolutional neural network (CNN) and geographically weighted regression (GWR) to explore the complex nonlinear relationship between environmental variables and extreme precipitation. The DGD framework was applied to downscale the CHM_PRE V2 daily precipitation product from 0.1° to 0.01° for an extreme rainfall event from August 2 to 6, 2023 in the black soil region of Northeast China and an unprecedented extreme precipitation event in Zhengzhou from July 17 to 22, 2021. Compared with random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGB), artificial neural network (ANN), GWR, CNN, and hybrid models including GWR-RF (GWRF) and GWR-XGB (GXGB), DGD achieved the best overall performance. DGD reduced the overestimation of light precipitation and underestimation of heavy precipitation while substantially suppressing the “boxy” artifacts commonly observed in RF, XGB, GWRF, and GXGB based results. Compared with the original CHM_PRE V2 product, the final downscaled results from DGD substantially enhanced the spatial detail of the original CHM_PRE V2 product while maintaining similar accuracy against rain gauge daily precipitation observations. Overall, the results indicate that the DGD framework driven by Sentinel-5P cloud physical parameters provides an effective approach for daily extreme precipitation downscaling, with potential applications in flood forecasting, hydrological modeling, and agricultural risk assessment.

title: Toward understanding tidal flat regime shifts: Contrasting hydro-sediment dynamics revealed by paired observations of two tidal flats
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Shibing Zhu, Ya Ping Wang, Yuan Li, Qingguang Zhu, Fei Xing, Mingliang Li, Chao Gao, Shucun Sun
abstract: Global muddy tidal flats are increasingly at risk of shifting from accretion-dominated to erosion-dominated states under the combined pressures of climate change and intensified human activities. Understanding the process basis of tidal flat regime shifts hinges on clarifying the fundamental differences in coupled hydrodynamics, sediment transport, and morphological processes that sustain erosional versus accretional states and their diagnostic implications. However, process-based studies that directly compare these contrasting states through paired observations within the same tidal flat system remain limited. Here, we conducted coordinated, high-frequency measurements of hydro-sediment processes at two morphologically contrasting sites—one eroding and one accreting—within the Jiangsu coast, China, which is experiencing a system-wide regime shift and exhibits strong spatial heterogeneity, with coexisting erosional and accretional sectors. Results show that the eroding flat experiences stronger wave forcing and higher bed shear stresses, which drive persistent seaward sediment export and ongoing bed erosion. In contrast, the wide and gently sloping morphology of the accreting flat enhances wave energy dissipation, promotes tidal current development, and generates early-flood velocity pulses that trigger SSC surges, creating critical sedimentation windows that sustain long-term accretion. Notably, SSC was higher at the eroding tidal flat than at the accreting site, underscoring that tidal flat regime shifts are not governed by sediment availability alone but rather emerge from complex interactions among morphology, hydrodynamics, and sediment transport processes. These findings advance process-based understanding of tidal flat evolution and provide mechanistic insights to support the management of coastal erosion risks under multiple stressors.

title: Global cropland expansion amplifies the risk of compound dry and hot events under climate change
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Haiyang Tu, Guoyong Leng, Linfei Yu, Lei Yao, Jiali Qiu, Lubin Han
abstract: Compound Dry and Hot Events (CDHEs) pose significant threats to global food security, with their frequency and severity projected to escalate under future climate change. However, the combined impacts of climate change and cropland expansion on CDHEs exposure across varying severity levels remain underexplored globally. Using climate model projections from CMIP6 and dynamic cropland maps under four Shared Socio-economic Pathways (SSPs), we assess global cropland exposure to CDHEs, categorized into mild, moderate, severe, extreme, and exceptional severities, and identify key drivers. Our findings reveal a consistent increase in global cropland exposure to CDHEs under all future warming scenarios, with exceptional CDHEs contributing the most significant rise (50.86% increase by 2070–2099), followed by moderate (15.23%), severe (14.43%), extreme (13.79%), and mild (5.69%) events. Northern South America, Sub-Saharan Africa, and parts of Asia face the largest exposure increases, exacerbating vulnerabilities due to limited adaptation capacity. Attribution analysis indicates that climate change drives exposure increases under SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5, while cropland expansion is the primary driver under SSP2-4.5 (contributing 42.24% by 2070–2099). Crucially, the interaction term becomes increasingly important, contributing 15–25% by 2070–2099 and rising with CDHEs severity, as new cropland is expanding into areas where CDHEs are intensifying rapidly. These findings highlight the urgent need for targeted climate mitigation and adaptive land-use policies to reduce CDHEs risks, particularly in vulnerable regions, to safeguard global food production.

title: Causal structure and threshold characteristics of vapor pressure deficit regulation across different climate zones in China
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Yang Han, Zhi-Gang Yan, Peng Zhou, Jia-Hui Qin, Chuan-Ye Hu, Yun-Cheng Jiang, Qing-Zhou Lv
abstract: Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD) is a key indicator of atmospheric aridity and land–atmosphere interaction risk, yet its dominant processes, information structure, and threshold responses across China’s climate zones remain poorly understood. Using VPD and related meteorological and hydrological variables during 1980–2022, this study grouped the drivers into Circulation Background (CB), Non-local Moisture Transport (NMT), and Local Response and Feedback (LRF), and integrated directional causality detection, information decomposition, and threshold analysis to reveal the dominant mechanisms and nonlinear responses of VPD in China. Mean VPD was 0.54 kPa, with high values in the northwestern inland and low values over the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau and the northeastern semi-humid region. VPD was highest in Mt-A (0.98 kPa) and lowest in Pt-Sa (0.25 kPa). The dominant controls showed clear zonal differentiation, with humid and semi-humid regions mainly controlled by CB, Mg-H by NMT, and arid and plateau regions by LRF; precipitation exerted the strongest causal effect in both Mt-A and Pt-Sa, with peak ρ values of 0.918 and 0.695. Information decomposition showed that CB and NMT were dominated by synergistic information (88.52% and 79.27% of pixels, respectively), whereas LRF showed a lower proportion of synergistic dominance (64.25%) but higher unique and redundant contributions (0.236 and 0.148). A total of 21 robust threshold relationships were identified, with more consistent response directions for local hydrological factors and stronger regional divergence for CB- and NMT-related variables. Overall, VPD in China is regulated by climate-zone-dependent control pathways rather than a single uniform mechanism, and the identified causal pathways and threshold responses provide a process-based basis for assessing regional atmospheric drying risk, diagnosing water-limitation transitions, and developing climate-zone-specific adaptation strategies.

title: Quantifying potential ground-ice meltwater release and seasonal active-layer water-storage change using decade-long InSAR-derived ground deformation in the Qilian Mountains
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Guanjun Wei, Hongyu Zhou, Guangrong Li, Hongwen Mu, Zhigang Du, Yu Li
abstract: Regional observation-based constraints on permafrost-degradation-driven hydrologic responses remain limited in the Qilian Mountains, especially for ground-ice meltwater release and active-layer seasonal water-storage change. Here we use decade-long Sentinel-1 InSAR time-series products (2014–2025) from the COMET-LiCSAR system to retrieve regional ground deformation and quantify two related hydrologic signals: (i) potential ground-ice meltwater release and (ii) active-layer seasonal exchangeable water-storage change. We combine multi-frame mosaicking, ascending/descending MSBAS decomposition, and time-series modeling to estimate long-term vertical deformation rates and time-varying seasonal deformation amplitudes within the mapped permafrost domain. The results indicate that long-term vertical deformation in the Qilian Mountains is dominated by weak background signals, although localized subsidence reaches approximately 30–40 mm/yr. The subsidence-based potential meltwater release is estimated as 7.94 × 107 m3/yr, equivalent to 0.42 mm/yr in runoff depth. After accounting for uplift, the conservative net volumetric change decreases to 3.22 × 10⁶ m3/yr, or 0.02 mm/yr. This small net signal is below the product-level uncertainty scale and should be interpreted as a near-zero deformation-derived constraint rather than a resolved runoff increase. Seasonal deformation amplitudes are mostly < 10 mm, and their interannual trends show spatially heterogeneous increases and decreases. These results indicate non-uniform changes in active-layer seasonal exchangeable water storage. Overall, the InSAR-constrained signals suggest that permafrost degradation in the Qilian Mountains is expressed more strongly as heterogeneous storage redistribution and seasonal regulation than as a coherent regional increase in net meltwater contribution to runoff.

title: Short-term changes in slope vegetation patch patterns and their regulation on sediment connectivity in an arid area
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Shangxuan Zhang, Long Li, Hairu Li, Linfu Liu, Yanan Ren, Yu Zhang
abstract: Vegetation patch patterns play a critical role in regulating surface hydrological processes in arid ecosystems. However, the short-term changes in these patterns and their coupling mechanisms with slope sediment connectivity (IC) remain poorly understood. In this study, we combined three years of in situ observations with Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) technologies to investigate the short-term dynamics of three vegetation patterns (random, uniform, and aggregated) and their impacts on soil erosion. The results showed that vegetation patch patterns exhibited signs of short-term degradation under erosive disturbance, characterized by increasingly complex patch boundaries, heightened fragmentation, and reduced functional connectivity. Specifically, the random pattern exhibited the most severe fragmentation, with the Landscape Shape Index (LSI) increasing by 27.76%. In terms of erosion regulation, the uniform pattern demonstrated the strongest runoff and sediment interception capacity, reducing runoff and sediment yield by 40.46% and 53.48%, respectively, compared with bare slopes. Furthermore, landscape metric analysis indicated that both LSI and COHESION were generally negatively associated with sediment connectivity (IC). The pattern-based prediction equations further showed that IC promoted runoff and sediment export, whereas CONNECT reduced erosion by interrupting continuous transport pathways. Collectively, our findings suggest that future ecological restoration management in arid regions should move beyond increasing vegetation coverage alone and optimize vegetation spatial configuration according to site water availability, vegetation stability, and the distribution of IC hotspots. Where site conditions permit, relatively uniform vegetation patterns may be considered to enhance runoff interception and sediment retention. Targeted interventions in high-IC areas may further help disrupt sediment connectivity, reduce runoff-driven sediment transport, and mitigate erosion risk.

title: Trace element sources, migration and health risks associated with river-groundwater interaction: Insights from isotopes, fluorescence spectroscopy and Monte Carlo simulation
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Xu Yang, Muhan Li, Yiying Miao, Fuyang Huang, Zeyuan Liu, Hongli Ma, Ping Miao, Jigang Shi, Zengbao Zhang, Shen Qu, Ruihong Yu
abstract: The sources, migration pathways, and associated risks of trace elements (TEs) linked to river–groundwater interactions remain inadequately understood. This study integrated a Bayesian isotope mixing model (MixSIAR), a 222Rn mass balance model (RMBM), and Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) to elucidate TE dynamics in the Hangjin Section of the Yellow River, China. Groundwater exhibited markedly higher TE concentrations than surface water, accompanied by higher values of the entropy-weighted water quality index (EWQI) and heavy metal pollution index (HPI). The MixSIAR results indicated that dissolved Sr compositions were jointly controlled by natural and anthropogenic hydrogeochemical processes, including evaporite dissolution (15.53%), silicate weathering (14.10%), carbonate weathering (11.70%), irrigation water (15.98%), sewage (15.43%), municipal water (15.52%), and fertilizers (11.74%), thereby influencing TE occurrence and enrichment in the study area. Fluorescence indices indicated that dissolved organic matter, primarily derived from terrestrial and microbial sources, significantly influenced TE behavior through complexation and adsorption processes, particularly in groundwater. Groundwater discharge-mediated fluxes, particularly Li (0.0595–0.3114 × 10‒4 g/(s∙m)), Mn (0.0508–0.5994 × 10‒4 g/(s∙m)), and Sr (3.5427–12.4769 × 10‒4 g/(s∙m)), substantially affected water quality of the Yellow River. Health risk assessments indicated considerable hazards associated with TE-contaminated groundwater, with children being more vulnerable than adults. Spatially, TE enrichment and health risks were generally greater in the upper reaches than in the middle and lower reaches, while TE migration exhibited element-specific spatial variability. This integrated approach improves our understanding of TE cycling mechanisms mediated by river–groundwater interactions and provides scientific guidance for water resource protection and public health.

title: HYDRO-XM: a computationally efficient, externally coupled, and flexible watershed model
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Menberu B. Meles, A.T.M. Sakiur Rahman, Jiří Šimůnek, Hoori Ajami, Carl L. Unkrich, Juan S. Acero Triana, Jason Goulding, Scott A. Bradford
abstract: Numerical simulation of watershed processes requires capturing the spatial and temporal dynamics of water movement, storage, and redistribution across surface and subsurface domains. We present HYDRO-XM, a computationally efficient, modular framework that couples three open-source models: KINEROS2 (K2) for overland and channel flow, HYDRUS-1D (H1D) for variably saturated flow in the unsaturated zone, and MODFLOW-5 (MF5) for saturated groundwater flow. The framework represents a watershed as a network of interconnected planar surface elements, channels, and storage units. Each surface element links to an H1D soil profile, which evaluates whether excess rainfall leads to runoff, receives information on ponded water available for infiltration from K2, and returns time-varying recharge fluxes to MF5. K2 solves the one-dimensional kinematic wave equation for surface and channel flow at event scale; H1D solves the Richards equation for vertical unsaturated flow; and MF5 computes three-dimensional saturated groundwater flow. HYDRO-XM replaces K2′s native Smith-Parlange infiltration scheme with Richards equation–based solutions from H1D, passing bottom-boundary fluxes to MF5 as distributed source/sink terms, allowing a continuous representation of water fluxes across the vadose zone–groundwater continuum within a fully coupled modeling framework. Key innovations include dynamic boundary-condition switching, which allows surface soil-column boundaries to transition automatically between flux-controlled and head-controlled states as saturation changes, adaptive time-stepping, dimensionality reduction, and parallelization that increases computational speed while preserving process fidelity. These features enable stable, continuous simulation of overland flow, channel flow, infiltration, soil moisture redistribution, and groundwater dynamics across full watershed domains. Benchmark cases using both idealized hypothetical domains and observed data from the Walnut Gulch Experimental Watershed show strong agreement with ParFlow, an integrated hydrologic model, outputs and field observations. Performance metrics ranged from NSE = 0.62–0.98, KGE = 0.24–0.93, and R 2 = 0.85–0.99 compared to observed streamflow, with water-balance errors below 3.4%. HYDRO-XM ran up to 28.4 times faster than a comparable ParFlow configuration. This framework provides a tractable tool for evaluating managed aquifer recharge, predicting hydrologic responses, and quantifying watershed-scale impacts of land-use change and climate variability.

title: Tracing hydrogeological sources of spring discharges to peat-forming bofedales in the Peruvian Andes
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Henry E. Moore, Alexander Avelar, Joaquin Cambeiro, Kristina Keating, Margaret Lang, Jasper Oshun
abstract: Peat-forming bofedales are unique environments found at high altitudes across the Peruvian Andes that provide critical ecosystem services such as sustaining streamflow to downslope communities. As limited studies have attempted to address seasonally dynamic groundwater flow from springs, we conducted a hydrogeophysical investigation to characterize and quantify specific discharges from springs over two weeks following the ‘wet-up’ period of two hydrogeologically distinct bofedales in the Upper Ramuschaka Watershed (Cusco, Perú). Handheld thermal infrared imagery and specific conductivity measurements were used to locate springs across the bofedales. Specific groundwater discharge rates were quantified with vertical temperature profilers installed in the springs. Ground-penetrating radar transects supported by coring revealed localized patterns in bedrock structure controlling peat thickness. Imaginary conductivity ( σ " ), and electrolytic conductivity ( σ el ), derived from time domain induced polarization, showed heterogenous deep bedrock structures around the springs and estimated the distribution of ionic fluid in the subsurface sourcing the springs. Hydrogeophysical results indicate three distinct spring types, which inform a conceptual model connecting the spring hydrology to underlying hydrogeological structure. This study examines the importance of bofedal springs in maintaining peat resources essential for the water resiliency of downstream communities.

title: Three-dimensional reservoir characterization from hard and soft data based on latent diffusion model
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Ce Zhang, Gang Liu, Qiyu Chen, Zhesi Cui, Hongfeng Fang, Dajie Chen, Junping Xiong, Kaikai Zhang
abstract: The reliability of three-dimensional (3D) reservoir modeling directly influences the accuracy of subsurface resource evaluation and development decisions. Traditional modeling methods primarily rely on sparse borehole data. Consequently, they struggle to fully integrate multi-source information, such as seismic interpretations. This leads to significant uncertainty in the modeling results. To address this issue, this study proposes a Soft-Hard Constrained Latent Diffusion Model (SH-LDM). This method integrates the hard data from boreholes and soft data from seismic interpretations to provide global structural information. It effectively constrains the modeling process, thereby enhancing model reliability. The SH-LDM first maps high-dimensional geological models into a low-dimensional latent space for learning and generation. This significantly reduces the complexity of model training and inference. Building on this, a conditional fusion strategy with multi-level feature embeddings is constructed. It simultaneously introduces the exact matching constraints of hard data and the trend guidance of soft data within the latent space. This achieves both strict control over hard data points and a coherent representation of the overall structural morphology. This study validates the effectiveness of the SH-LDM on non-stationary 2D and 3D reservoir datasets. The consistency of the generated model with training images in both local and global features is evaluated using the minimum acceptance criterion. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons with various benchmark models demonstrate the superior performance of the SH-LDM in terms of modeling accuracy and statistical consistency. Ablation studies and sensitivity analyses demonstrate that incorporating soft data significantly enhances the reliability of modeling results. Furthermore, the SH-LDM exhibits a certain degree of robustness to noise present in the soft data.

title: A neighborhood change detection method for soil moisture retrieval using single-temporal Sentinel-1 data over vegetated fields
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Qi Dou, Jie Yang, Weidong Sun, Lingli Zhao, Lei Shi, Hongtao Shi, Chuang Liu, Jiaxin Qian, Qinghua Xie
abstract: The short-term change detection (STCD) method obviates the need for complex modeling of surface and vegetation scattering processes, providing a simple and efficient means for large-scale soil moisture estimation from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data. However, due to the reliance on prior assumptions and densely observed time-series data, the STCD method is susceptible to temporal variations in surface roughness and vegetation, and may introduce delays in generating stable retrieval results through a temporal sliding window. This study proposes a neighborhood change detection (NCD) method that incorporates spatial information into the retrieval framework. Instead of assuming parameter invariance over time, the NCD method transfers this assumption to the spatial domain. By constructing a system of equations based on observations from a target pixel and its neighboring pixels, the method enables soil moisture retrieval using a single-temporal SAR image. To mitigate the effects of spatial heterogeneity in vegetation, homogeneous pixels are selected based on the similarity of target scattering characteristics. A weighting strategy is then applied to the constructed linear system to enhance retrieval stability. Considering the uncertainty inherent in the underdetermined parameter estimation process, physical bounds derived from passive microwave soil moisture products are used to constrain and optimize the solution. The validation results based on C-band Sentinel-1 data and in situ measurements demonstrate that the proposed NCD method achieves retrieval performance comparable to the traditional STCD approach, despite the limited information provided by a single-temporal acquisition. The retrieval results yield root mean square errors of 0.068 m3/m3 and 0.072 m3/m3 for the two soil moisture monitoring networks, with correlation coefficients of 0.74 and 0.58, respectively. Moreover, the NCD method exhibits particularly strong robustness under conditions of relatively low soil moisture and limited variability in its temporal dynamics. The proposed NCD algorithm further reduces the complexity of data acquisition and processing, offering a complementary alternative for near real-time soil moisture mapping in support of emergency applications.

title: Time-series decomposition and stream metabolism reveal benthic control on particulate organic carbon transport from mixed-use Appalachian watersheds
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): William I. Ford, James Fox, Mindy Armstead, Andrea Erhardt
abstract: Algal carbon can be a significant energy source in stream ecosystems; however, knowledge is lacking regarding algal contributions to particulate organic carbon (POC) fluxes from mixed-use stream ecosystems and their potential implications for downstream waterways. We report a new four-year transported carbon elemental and isotopic dataset from a predominantly forested stream ecosystem in northwestern West Virginia, USA, carry out time series decomposition of the data, and compare our results to algae monitoring and ecosystem modelling to better understand the influence of algal carbon on these systems. Results show that variational mode decomposition (VMD) was more effective than empirical mode decomposition (EMD) for detecting in-stream process impacts on POC transport in the forested stream. Results from ecosystem modelling and significant modes from VMD point to benthic algal growth followed by heterotrophic stabilization resulting in residual algal C transport from the watershed during storm events as POC. The importance of the time lag and then carbon flux introduced by the algal stabilization process extends this paradigm to be inclusive of both open-canopied systems studied previously and predominantly closed-canopy systems, such as the one studied here. Contrary to results from open-canopy systems, the mixed-use Appalachian stream shows dual-peaks of algal carbon conveyance, starting in late winter-spring and again in late-summer to mid fall. Results provide evidence that mixed-use watersheds in Appalachia provide periodic contributions of labile POC enriched in algal C to the Ohio River, USA and thus merit further study regarding potential impacts on eutrophication and harmful algal blooms in the regulated rivers.

title: Hydrological drivers of silicate weathering in snow-dominated alpine headwater catchments with variable forest cover (Tatra Mountains, Western Carpathians)
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Agnieszka Rajwa-Kuligiewicz, Artur Kuligiewicz, Marek Duliński, Kazimierz Różański
abstract: This study quantifies silicate weathering rates (SWR) and carbon dioxide capture rates (CCR) in mid-latitude mountains with seasonal snow cover, with particular focus on snowmelt-driven weathering and vegetation effects. The study was conducted in headwater catchments within the crystalline core of the Tatra Mountains (Carpathians), which share similar lithology but differ in forest cover and disturbance history. The study combined geochemical modeling with isotope-based analyses, including mean transit time (MTT) estimation using stable water isotopes and tritium, together with mixing–splitting analysis. The tritium-derived MTT was ∼3.7 years, reflecting dominant winter baseflow conditions, whereas MTT estimated from the sine-wave method yielded much shorter times (0.4–2.4 years), likely due to stronger relative contribution of shorter flow paths. Mean SWR ranged from 5.19 ± 0.14 t/km2/yr to 7.60 ± 0.29 t/km2/yr, while CCR ranged from 2.58 ± 0.23 × 104 to 3.76 ± 0.33 × 104 mol/km2/yr. The results indicate a kinetically limited weathering regime in which reaction kinetics and MTT exert stronger controls on weathering fluxes than discharge or catchment area. SWR and dissolution rates varied among catchments, with the forested catchment exhibiting higher weathering rates, longer MTT, lower young water fractions, and greater contribution of winter precipitation to summer discharge. Mean annual evapotranspiration (ET) ranged from ∼42% in the mature forest to ∼60% in the regenerating stand. Because summer precipitation with a relatively high 18O/16O ratio was preferentially lost to ET, the isotopic composition of water contributing to weathering was biased towards winter precipitation with a relatively low 18O/16O ratio.

title: Modeling nutrient-driven water quality changes in Miyun Reservoir: An improved SWAT–Delft3D approach
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Yan Jiang, Yiping Chen, Lijing Pang, Zhengfang Huang, Hongtao Zhao, Xuefeng Wu
abstract: Excessive nutrient input severely degrades reservoir water quality, yet reservoir responses to terrestrial pollution sources remain poorly quantified. This study developed an integrated watershed–reservoir simulation framework by coupling the SWAT model with the Delft3D model, where the Delft3D river module replaced SWAT’s channel routing module to better represent hydrological connectivity and nutrient transport across the overland–river–reservoir continuum.
