However, mass balance consistency analysis reveals that this apparent increase is a concentration effect due to soil mass loss rather than a net carbon stock gain. In contrast, medium- to high-intensity erosion (≥ 0.24 m/s) causes aggregates breakdown and 25–30% SOC loss (r > 0.89). Our model delivers high prediction accuracy (R2 > 0.90), and sensitivity analysis confirms that D is the dominant parameter (S1 = 0.51; St = 0.83). Compared with empirical and process-based models, this approach greatly improves SOC prediction under dynamic erosion by explicitly distinguishes concentration effects from stock changes, providing a more credible interpretation of the system as a carbon source. We reveal that low-intensity erosion induces a transient enrichment of SOC concentration rather than a net carbon sink, whereas high-intensity erosion generates substantial carbon sources. Employing fractal dimension as a core predictor, our mechanistic model improves carbon cycle assessments and supports soil conservation and climate strategies.

title: Deep learning-based downscaling of SMAP data for surface and root-zone soil moisture mapping
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Saman Rabiei, Ebrahim Babaeian, Sabine Grunwald
abstract: Accurate soil moisture (SM) information at sub-kilometer resolution is essential for hydrologic modeling, weather forecasting, precision irrigation, and drought monitoring. Satellite missions such as Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) have transformed global SM monitoring, but their coarse resolution, shallow sensing depth, and multi-day revisit cycle limit local-scale applications. Retrieval accuracy further declines over dense vegetation and complex terrain. This study presents a deep learning downscaling framework that integrates convolutional neural networks and long short-term memory networks (CNN-LSTM) to produce daily SM maps at 100 m resolution for surface (5 cm) and root-zone (20 cm) depths. The model was trained with seven years of SM data from ∼ 650 stations across the U.S., using dynamic predictors from SMAP and MODIS (i.e., brightness temperature, roughness coefficient, surface reflectance in red, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared) and static features predictors from elevation, land cover, and Soil Landscapes of the U.S. (SOLUS100) databases. Compared to SMAP level-3 SM, the CNN-LSTM improved surface SM accuracy, with median correlation coefficient (R) increasing from 0.61 to 0.82, unbiased root mean square error (ubRMSE) decreasing from 0.06 to 0.05 cm3 cm−3, and Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE) increasing from 0.30 to 0.61. Root-zone SM achieved R ∼ 0.72, ubRMSE ∼ 0.05 cm3 cm−3 and KGE ∼ 0.53. The model also outperformed SMAP in forested and mountainous areas, capturing SMAP sub-pixel SM variability across the three well-instrumented watersheds and Florida. In Florida, where no training data was used, performance decreased but was still better than SMAP. These findings indicate that the CNN-LSTM framework bridges the spatial resolution gap in SM products and support small scale agricultural and hydrological applications.

title: A unified framework for groundwater level imputation and forecasting in data-limited catchments
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Yaggesh Kumar Sharma, Seokhyeon Kim, Ashish Sharma, Okke Batelaan
abstract: Accurate groundwater-level forecasting is essential for sustainable water management, yet remains challenging in data-scarce regions where monitoring records are incomplete and discontinuous. This study examines whether reliable forecasts can be achieved when training data are substantially reconstructed rather than fully observed. To address this problem, we developed a Groundwater Level–Imputation–Forecasting (GWL-IMFO) framework that combines Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) with Neural Architecture Search (NAS). MICE was used to reconstruct missing monthly groundwater-level records, while NAS selected suitable ANN, LSTM, or GRU-based forecasting architectures under imputation-affected data conditions. The framework was evaluated across 1,493 monitoring wells in six basins representing diverse aquifer types, land-use/land-cover classes, and Köppen climate zones. Controlled missing-data scenarios of 20%, 30%, and 40% were generated only within the 2005–2023 training period, while 2024 observations were kept independent for out-of-sample forecasting evaluation. The 40% missing-data scenario was used as a stress-test condition to assess robustness under severe monitoring-data degradation. Even under this condition, GWL-IMFO maintained useful short- to mid-term forecasting skill, achieving median correlation values above 0.60 and RMSE below 1 m for forecasts up to 12 months, and outperforming conventional LSTM, GRU, and ANN models in most cases. These results indicate that model architectures trained on reconstructed groundwater records should not be assumed fixed a priori, but may need to adapt to imputation-affected data characteristics. The proposed framework provides a reproducible and scalable benchmark for groundwater forecasting in heterogeneous, data-limited environments, while also highlighting the need to consider data completeness, missing-data severity, hydrogeological setting, and forecast horizon when applying the model operationally.

title: A review of machine learning applications in inland and nearshore water color remote sensing: from preprocessing to object detection and parameter estimation
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Jiarui Shi, Zuchuan Li, Ge Liu, Chong Fang, Zhidan Wen, Yingxin Shang, Hui Tao, Sijia Li, Qiang Wang, Zijin Wang, Kaishan Song
abstract: A combination of Machine Learning (ML) techniques with satellite remote sensing has brought target objects and water-quality research into a new era. These emerging techniques and unprecedented opportunities have improved the accuracy of satellite data products, facilitated knowledge discovery, expanded the spatial domain of target objects and water-quality research to the globe, and extended the social, economic, and scientific impacts of water-quality research. This review provides the first systematic integration of machine learning (ML) across the full-chain workflow for inland and nearshore watercolor remote sensing, we examine recent progress in the application of ML across the full remote sensing workflow for inland and nearshore water color studies—from image preprocessing (including atmospheric correction, water body extraction, spectral simulation, spatiotemporal fusion and water extent extraction) to object detection and water quality parameter estimation. We also present a curated selection of valuable open-source resources and highlight key challenges—including data scarcity and label bias, limited model interpretability, insufficient uncertainty quantification, and the difficulties of multimodal data integration, long-term, large-scale, and multi-scale analysis, as well as the need for effective spatial relationship modeling—and discuss emerging trends such as multi-temporal data integration, and the incorporation of physical constraints. By providing a comprehensive overview of ML applications in this field, this review serves as a valuable reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to enhance water quality monitoring and assessment. The insights presented here are expected to foster the development of more accurate, scalable, and interpretable ML models, ultimately contributing to improved environmental management and decision-making.

title: A critical evaluation of water balance in the Yellow River Source Region
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part C Author(s): Boya Han, Yuefei Huang, Shuo Zhang
abstract: Most hydrological models assume that water is balanced within topographic basin boundaries, but this basin-closure assumption is rarely critically evaluated, especially in the Yellow River Source Region (YRSR). Here we evaluate water-balance closure for the YRSR upstream of Tangnaihai by combining two complementary lines of evidence: a multi-source water-balance diagnosis based on independent products of precipitation, evapotranspiration, observed runoff, and terrestrial water storage for 1984–2020, and a process-based modified abcd (Mabcd) simulation that explicitly represents groundwater storage and intercatchment exchange. Because uncertainties in precipitation, evapotranspiration, and storage change remain substantial, the exact annual imbalance cannot be robustly determined for individual years from the water-balance residual alone. We therefore focus on residual features that are consistent across product combinations, and with simulation results using the Mabcd model which independently reproduces the same seasonal structure and long-term tendency, and yields an interbasin groundwater-flow estimate of the same order of magnitude as the ensemble residual. Taken together, the diagnostic water-balance evidence and the process-based Mabcd results suggest that groundwater exchange is a plausible, but highly uncertain, explanation for the observed residual structure. These results therefore motivate explicit testing of groundwater exchange in YRSR water-resource models.

title: Monitoring monthly water storage variation of the Three Gorges Reservoir using SWOT observations
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Qiye Sun, Hui Li, Yonggui Wang
abstract: Reservoir storage dynamics are essential for water resources management but remain difficult to quantify in elongated riverine reservoirs where longitudinal water surface gradients violate the horizontal-surface assumption commonly adopted in conventional estimation methods. This study presents a novel Water Volume plus Compensation Volume (WV + CV) framework that explicitly accounts for non-uniform water surface morphology in elongated riverine reservoirs. Leveraging wide-swath observations from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission, we reconstructed spatially continuous longitudinal water surface profiles for the Three Gorges Reservoir (August 2023-August 2025) and, for the first time, integrated two-dimensional water surface structure into reservoir storage estimation. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on the horizontal-surface assumption, the proposed WV + CV method decomposes storage change into water volume and compensation volume terms, thereby reducing systematic volumetric biases caused by pronounced longitudinal water level gradients. The method was evaluated against conventional trapezoidal and area--elevation--volume approaches. Results show that the reservoir experiences pronounced seasonal transitions between quasi-horizontal and strongly sloped water surface configurations, particularly during flood-season regulation. Under intensified longitudinal gradients, conventional methods systematically underestimate storage variations, whereas the WV + CV approach demonstrates strong agreement with reference estimates (R2 = 0.970; RMSE = 0.929 km3). These findings highlight the importance of resolving two-dimensional water surface structure for reliable storage estimation in elongated reservoirs and demonstrate the capability of SWOT observations to capture reservoir-scale water surface morphology, providing a scalable framework for monitoring storage dynamics in similar riverine reservoirs.

title: Vegetation-hydrology interactions modulate porewater salinity dynamics in coastal salt marshes
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Lucheng Zhan, Qi Xu, Jiaying Liang, Xiaodong He, Jiaheng Yan
abstract: Coastal salt marshes are vital ecosystems vulnerable to salinity conditions affected by complex intertidal hydrology. Although water-salt dynamics under tidal and climatic variations are well studied, the dynamic role of marsh vegetation in regulating porewater salinity remains insufficiently understood. This study integrates field monitoring of soil bulk electrical conductivity (EC) with controlled experiments to assess how upper intertidal vegetation influences bulk-EC-inferred porewater salinity dynamics, using Spartina alterniflora as a representative marsh species. At the field site, vegetated soils exhibited consistently more variable and lower bulk EC, with the mean EC at 1.0 m depth ∼20% lower than in adjacent bare flats. Controlled tank experiments further showed that rainwater infiltration reduced porewater salinity by up to 80.7% in vegetated plots, compared with 70.1% in bare soils within 37 days. The ∼10% difference in salinity change ratio (SCR) persisted for more than two months during subsequent dry conditions dominated by evaporation. These results suggest that marsh vegetation enhances the utilization of episodic rainwater inputs and promotes vertical salt leaching, while also moderating evaporation-driven salinization during dry periods. Overall, the findings indicate that marsh vegetation can modulate porewater salinity dynamics and help maintain suitable root-zone conditions during the growing season. These vegetation-mediated effects may contribute to the stability of coastal wetlands, although their persistence across seasons and longer timescales requires further investigation.

title: Inter-reservoir benefit compensation for water-sediment regulation in the Yellow River Basin: From status quo to multi-functional synergy
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Hao Hu, Guiliang Tian, Jan Franklin Adamowski, Mohammad Reza Alizadeh, Xiaodong Yan, Qingqing Ban
abstract: To promote multi-objective synergy of water‑sediment regulation in the Yellow River Basin (YRB), this study develops an “optimization‑guided, compensation‑driven” regulation framework. A multi-objective collaborative model adaptable to various hydrological scenarios is established as the core analytical foundation. On this basis, a dual-track benefit compensation mechanism is formulated as the implementation driver, comprising horizontal impact-feedback compensation and vertical gap-filling compensation. Applied across three hydrological years (2018: wet year with high sediment load; 2013: normal year with medium sediment load; 2017: dry year with low sediment load), the model was tested on the Sanmenxia-Xiaolangdi reservoir system and the downstream channel as a case study. Results indicate that the majority of Pareto-optimal solutions fell within the range of primary to good coupling coordination, validating the model’s effectiveness. Analysis of inter-objective relationships reveals a complex trade-off structure: sediment discharge and reduction benefits compete strongly with hydropower generation benefits and weakly with ecological water deficit losses, whereas hydropower generation benefits and ecological water deficit losses exhibit significant synergy. Compared to actual operations, the synergistic approach increased total system benefits by 0.365 × 109 CNY (2018), 0.200 × 109 CNY (2013), and 0.131 × 109 CNY (2017), respectively. Following the implementation of a compensation mechanism, all stakeholders retained benefits equal to or greater than their actual levels, ensuring the scheme’s acceptability. The model provides a quantifiable approach to addressing interest imbalance and theoretical support for transitioning towards multi-functional synergy in YRB’s WSR.

title: Regional process-based analysis of trends in flood peaks and volumes using hourly data
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Yves Tramblay, Patrick Arnaud, Pierre Javelle
abstract: Most studies on flood trends rely on daily discharge data at the station scale, limiting their ability to disentangle contrasting trends in different flood-generation mechanisms. This is particularly true for capturing short-duration processes such as flash floods. Here, we propose a process-based regional framework to investigate trends across different flood types using hourly data. We analyze 829 small to medium-sized catchments (<500 km2) across France using hourly discharge, radar rainfall, and reanalysis-based soil moisture data. Flood events are extracted using a peaks-over-threshold approach and classified into four categories based on response time (flash vs. slow) and antecedent soil moisture conditions (saturated vs. non-saturated). Catchments are grouped into four homogeneous hydro-climatic regions, and a spatio-temporal declustering procedure is applied to account for spatial and temporal dependence between concurrent events. Trends in flood peaks and direct runoff volumes are then assessed using regional quantile regression. Results reveal strong contrasts between regions and flood types. Only a few trends were detected for flood peaks, whereas flood volumes exhibit more frequent significant increasing trends. The strongest increases are found for flash flood volumes in mountainous and Mediterranean regions. For slow-onset floods, significant positive volume trends are observed in basins located in temperate regions, in line with increases in both rainfall totals and duration. Overall, flood volumes show a systematically higher sensitivity to change than peak flows. These findings demonstrate that flood trend detection critically depends on temporal resolution, flood type, and regional context, and that volume-based metrics provide complementary and often stronger signals than peak-based indicators for assessing evolving flood hazards.

title: Microfracture network connectivity controls oil–water imbibition in 3D matrix-microfracture systems: a pore-scale investigation with percolation theory
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Peiyu Li, Zhaojie Song, Yilei Song, Xiukun Wang, Japan Trivedi, Jiaqi Wang, Zhe Li
abstract: Oil-water imbibition in matrix-microfracture systems is a key mechanism governing fluid transport in subsurface multiphase flow. Although recent studies have highlighted the critical role of fracture connectivity in imbibition, most of them treat microfracture connectivity in a qualitative manner and do not establish a quantitative criterion—when microfracture network becomes connected and how the imbibition mechanism transitions after connectivity is achieved. To address this problem, we built an integrated pore-scale framework that couples percolation theory with pore-scale imbibition simulations. Three-dimensional multiscale models spanning a wide range of fracture densities are constructed, and oil-water imbibition is simulated using a multi-relaxation-time lattice Boltzmann method (MRT-LBM). A Monte Carlo analysis is then performed to determine the critical percolation threshold, which occurs at a dimensionless fracture density of 4.5. In non-percolating matrix-microfracture networks, isolated microfractures act as local dead ends, and matrix-dominated imbibition leaves residual oil near fracture tips and in poorly accessible matrix regions. In percolating networks (the dimensionless fracture density from 4.3 to 6.0), connected microfractures provide fast pathways for wetting phase invasion and oil drainage; the increased geometric complexity and network connectivity intensify counter-current matrix-microfracture imbibition and reduced absolute residual oil saturation by 12.25%. However, the oil saturation response to microfracture density is non-monotonic: excessively high microfracture densities promote water channeling, hinder matrix-microfracture fluid exchange, and ultimately reduce recovery. By identifying microfracture network connectivity as the critical control on imbibition regime transitions, this work provides new fluid dynamics insight into matrix-microfracture fluid exchange and multiphase flow behavior in fractured porous media.

title: Unraveling the rainfall-waterlogging propagation lag in urban systems: mechanisms, response patterns, and source tracking evidence
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Baojun Guan, Jingming Hou, Donglai Li, Yanhong Wang, Xinxin Pan, Jiahao Lv, Chenchen Fan, Guangzhao Chen, Liping Ma, Tian Wang
abstract: Real-time forecasting of urban waterlogging is frequently hindered by the complex spatiotemporal mismatch between rainfall inputs and hydrological response, defined here as the Rainfall-Waterlogging Propagation Lag (RWPL). Although hydrodynamic modeling is widely employed, the physical mechanisms underlying the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of RWPL remain poorly understood, largely because conventional models lack the capability to track runoff sources and pathways. To bridge this gap, this study investigates the non-linear dynamics of RWPL using a high-performance coupled model (GAST-SWMM) integrated with a fully 1D-2D coupled Rainfall Time-Source Tracking (TST) module. Combining theoretical benchmarks established via idealized models with a case study of the Xi’an Moat Basin, we identified three distinct physical response patterns of urban waterlogging: (1) Topography-dominated pattern: characterized by a monotonic decrease in RWPL with increasing rainfall intensity, driven by the rapid concentration of overland flow waves. (2) Dynamic connectivity pattern: exhibiting a non-monotonic trend where RWPL initially increases then decreases with rainfall intensity. This reveals a fill-and-spill mechanism governed by explicit quantitative thresholds, where catchment expansion elongates flow paths and causes significant delays. (3) Pipe-buffering pattern: controlled by hydraulic blockage. The transition from free surface flow to pressurized pipe flow creates a buffering effect, decoupling surface inundation from rainfall peaks. Crucially, the coupled TST fingerprints provide robust quantitative evidence validating these mechanisms. These findings challenge the static catchment assumptions in traditional forecasting and provide a theoretical basis for a dynamic offline-online predictive framework, advancing the transition from rainfall monitoring to precise impact forecasting.

title: Integrating multi-source remote sensing and numerical simulation approaches for enhanced flood hazard assessment
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Ebrahim Hamidi, Brad G. Peter, Behzad Nazari, Hamed Moftakhari, Katherine Anarde, Hamid Moradkhani
abstract: Extreme flooding is expected to intensify under a warming climate, which emphasizes the need for rapid and accurate flood mapping to support effective risk assessment. Remote sensing (RS) and numerical simulations (NS) are widely used for flood monitoring, yet both have limitations that introduce uncertainty. NS rely on gauge observations for calibration, reducing accuracy in poorly gauged areas. RS offers spatially continuous coverage, especially in unmonitored regions, but is often hindered by cloud cover, vegetation, and low temporal resolution, frequently missing peak flood events and reducing mapping precision. In this study, we integrate multi-source RS data, including optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, with NS to improve the characterization of extreme floods. RS data provide high-resolution flood extent maps that support verification and calibration of NS models. In turn, NS offers process-based, high-temporal-resolution flood maps and flood dynamics information (e.g., flood depths), which are critical for emergency response. We assess this integrated approach through two case studies: the 2019 flood in Coffeyville, Kansas, and the 2017 Hurricane Harvey flood on the Texas coast. In Coffeyville, a model calibrated using gauge data was validated with RS flood maps. In the data-scarce Texas case, model calibration was based on satellite-derived flood extents. Results show up to 98% agreement between simulated and RS-based maps, though either singular method may occasionally yield unreliable outputs. This integrated approach leverages the complementary strengths of the two approaches to provide decision-makers with more reliable and higher resolution flood data for effective response to the expected extreme events.

title: ZY1-02D satellite spectral inversion of organic matter in highland mountainous red soils based on electric eel optimisation feature extraction and hybrid liquid neural network fusion
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Chengbiao Fu, Zexin Zhang, Anhong Tian
abstract: Soil serves as the pivotal hub of terrestrial carbon cycling, and the full realisation of its carbon sequestration potential can contribute to mitigating global climate change. Variations in soil organic matter influence the global carbon cycle, with its quantity and quality directly determining soil productivity and sustainable utilisation levels. This study investigates the highland red soils of Dongchuan District, Kunming City, Yunnan Province, China. Utilising ground-based ASD hyperspectral and ZY1-02D satellite hyperspectral imagery as data sources, a multi-branch deep prediction model (M-LNN) incorporating liquid neural networks is proposed for quantitative inversion of red soil organic matter content. This model effectively extracts local spectral features, continuous dynamic characteristics, and long-term dependency information from hyperspectral data, thereby enhancing the prediction accuracy of organic matter. It incorporates multiple network architectures, employing parallel fusion of CNN, LNN, LSTM, and GRU networks to address limitations of LNN in hyperspectral inversion. Attention mechanisms are incorporated into each branch to refine the M-LNN, while multiple strategies enhance the traditional IEEFO algorithm to identify organic matter-sensitive spectral bands. The model demonstrated robust performance on ASD data with R2 = 0.8175, RMSE = 8.4713, RPD = 2.3410, and RPIQ = 2.4731. On ZY1-02D data, it achieved R2 = 0.5708, RMSE = 12.7520, RPD = 1.5264, and RPIQ = 2.5212, due to limitations in satellite spectral resolution, atmospheric interference, and surface heterogeneity, this level of accuracy is considered moderate, and the model’s ability to generalize to satellite data still needs to be further improved. Concurrently, SHAP analysis confirms the interpretability of the proposed IEEFO algorithm for screening organic matter-sensitive bands, and maps the spatial distribution of organic matter in red soils. This study provides a novel framework for predicting organic matter content in Yunnan Plateau red soils, offering scientific data references for regional soil fertility assessment and precision agricultural decision-making.

title: Assessments of eight ET products based on long-term multi-source water balance elements in 133 catchments across China
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Xiangyong Fu, Changming Li, Hanbo Yang
abstract: Accurate quantification of evapotranspiration (ET) is crucial for understanding hydrological processes in a changing environment. However, existing global ET products exhibit notable inconsistencies in regional ET representation and its trends, particularly in China. Previous studies, constrained by limited long-term runoff data, have not comprehensively assessed the performance of ET products in long-term trend representation. In addition, previous water balance-based assessments, which rely on single input data, generally have relatively large uncertainty. Therefore, we evaluated eight ET products, namely Collocation-Analyzed Multi-source Ensembled Land Evapotranspiration (CAMELE-0.25° and CAMELE-0.1°), ECMWF Reanalysis v5-Land (ERA5L), Global Land Data Assimilation System (GLDAS), Global Land Evaporation Amsterdam Model (GLEAM), MODIS Global Evapotranspiration Product (MOD16), FLUXCOM, and Penman-Monteith-Leuning Evapotranspiration Version 2 (PMLV2), in 133 catchments across China during1980-2016 using a multi-source input water balance method. To corroborate these findings, an independent evaluation was also conducted using observations from 32 flux stations in China. The results indicated that both assessment methods yielded consistent conclusions, i.e., all products overestimating monthly and annual ET. Among these, GLEAM and PMLV2 generally exhibited better performance. Their performance varied regionally, with higher accuracy in northern China and larger uncertainties in southern China. Additionally, the products showed significant differences in capturing long-term ET trends, particularly in spatial distribution of the trends. Among them, GLEAM demonstrated the highest accuracy in trend estimation. This study advances the understanding of land surface ET datasets and provides guidance for selecting regionally appropriate ET products across China, thereby supporting informed hydrological studies and decision-making application.

title: A deep learning-based probabilistic framework for streamflow prediction and water quality assessment
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Alberto Mena, Rafael J. Bergillos, Javier Paredes-Arquiola, Gerald Corzo, Abel Solera, Joaquín Andreu
abstract: This study presents an integrated modelling framework designed to support water quality assessment and regulatory compliance analysis in river basins. The proposed approach combines deep learning-based streamflow prediction, stochastic uncertainty propagation, hydrological spatial disaggregation, and process-based water quality modelling at the basin scale. The framework is applied to the Júcar River Basin (eastern Spain), a highly regulated Mediterranean system characterized by strong hydrological variability and significant water quality pressures. Streamflow is predicted using a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, and uncertainty is propagated through Monte Carlo simulations to generate ensemble inflow predictions. These inflows are spatially disaggregated using variation factors derived from an HBV hydrological model, providing distributed inputs to a water quality model that simulates concentrations of biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), phosphorus, and ammonium. The framework successfully reproduces the main spatial and temporal patterns of pollutant concentrations while explicitly quantifying the uncertainty associated with hydrological predictions. Water chemical status classifications show high agreements with observations, achieving accuracies of 90% for BOD, 84.4% for phosphorus, and 85.3% for ammonium. By providing probabilistic estimates of pollutant concentrations, the framework also enables identification of periods with elevated risk of regulatory threshold exceedance. Overall, the proposed approach offers a robust and transferable methodology for integrating probabilistic hydrological forecasting with water quality assessment, supporting risk-informed river basin management under uncertainty.

title: Physical-guided hybrid modelling framework for hydropower forecasting in non-stationary cascade reservoir systems
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Nan Wu, Liangang Chen, Zhongrui Ning, Yong Shi, Jerker Jarsjö, Ke Zhang
abstract: In cascade reservoir systems, generation discharge is jointly influenced by hydroclimatic conditions and operating strategies. Accurate forecasting is therefore essential for safe operation and improved production benefits. We developed a physical-informed hybrid generation discharge forecasting framework, LSTM-PHY. It applies BFAST to decompose the hydropower generation (power) series into trend, seasonal, and residual components. Each component is modeled separately and then converted to generation discharge using the hydropower conversion equation. We evaluated LSTM-PHY at two major reservoirs in the Yalong River cascade system: Ertan and Jinping-I. The results show that: (1) BFAST produced physically consistent components: the trend captures the long-term evolution of regulation strategies, the seasonal term reflects monsoon-driven inflow patterns and within-year cycles, and the residual represents high-frequency variability induced by short-term scheduling decisions; the detected breakpoints are physically interpretable. (2) LSTM modeled the residual series well, achieving coefficient of determination R 2 = 0.87 for Ertan in both the Calibration and Validation periods. For Jinping-I reached 0.82 in Calibration but decreased to 0.75 in Validation, indicating that training length affects generalization. (3) For generation discharge, LSTM-PHY achieved NSE = 0.90 in Calibration, outperforming LSTM-only (0.74) and BFAST-only (0.68). At the monthly scale, it maintained stable high performance in both flood and non-flood seasons, showing that physical-informed deep learning can capture seasonal discharge dynamics. Overall, LSTM-PHY improves predictive skill while providing a physically meaningful multi-scale view of cascade regulation, supporting hydropower forecasting and adaptive management under climate change.

title: Moisture transport patterns over the Northeastern Tibetan Plateau revealed by tree-ring δ 18 O records
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Kai Wang, Xiaohua Gou, Takeshi Nakatsuka, Yiran Zhang, Jiangzhou Feng, Linlin Gao, Tao Wang, Yang Deng, Zhen Li, Kaixuan Yang, Xuan Li, Chongshan Wang, Zibo Wang, Dingcai Yin
abstract: Understanding moisture transport in monsoon–westerly transition zones is critical for interpreting hydroclimatic change in arid and semi-arid regions. The northeastern Tibetan Plateau lies at the boundary between monsoon- and westerly-dominated systems, yet the relative roles of different moisture sources remain debated. Here, we developed six tree-ring cellulose oxygen isotope (δ18Otree) chronologies spanning ∼100 years from Qinghai spruce along an east–west transect and analyzed their climatic signals using multivariate statistics and reanalysis data. The records show strong spatial structure and cluster into eastern, central, and western groups with distinct controls. Eastern, central, and western sites exhibit distinct δ18Otree patterns that are most consistent with differing hydroclimatic influences: southeastern monsoon-related moisture at the eastern sites, easterly transport associated with the Mongolian anticyclone at the central sites, and a stronger westerly influence with additional anticyclonic modulation at the western sites. Results suggest an eastward shift in the effective expression of monsoon influence and a westward expansion of easterly moisture transport over the past century, consistent with regional warming–wetting since the 1980 s. The multi-site δ18Otree network provides new proxy-based evidence for moisture-source dynamics in this transition zone.

title: Particle and carbon export from a restored goldmine in an Amazonian catchment: hydro-sedimentary source tracing
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Naomi Nitschke, Stéphane Guédron, Cedric Legout, Antonio Martinez-Cortizas, Stanislav Jelavic, Jennifer Harris, Emmanuel Tessier, Sylvain Campillo, Stéphane Taravella, David Amouroux
abstract: Artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM) is prevalent in South America and the Amazon. It involves soil reworking, leading to an increase in downstream river turbidity and ecosystem degradation. In French Guiana, restoration, including landscaping and tree-replanting, is mandatory for legal gold mines, but the fate of post-exploitation sites is poorly characterised. To investigate the extent of particle export originating from a restored gold-mining site, high frequency suspended solid concentrations (SSC) and discharge measurements were performed upstream and downstream of a site in French Guiana. Two flood events were followed with geochemical tracers involving multielemental concentrations and Fourier-transformed infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) data in the particulate and filtered fractions, to unravel the origin of water (overland flow and groundwater), and particles (forest topsoil, mine topsoil, or riverbed sediments) within the watershed. Results show that within the year following restoration, the mining site remains a significant source of particles and carbon to the river, with an excess 100–300 kg km−2 (1.5–2.4 times increase) of particles exported due to the mining site, and specific carbon exports amounting to 9.8 ± 0.6 tCyr−1 km−2, comparable to exports observed in larger watersheds in the Amazon region. Hydrogeochemical and mineralogical data in the particulate fraction hint towards riverbank erosion and riverbed sediment remobilisation as an important source of suspended particles rather than mining site surface erosion. This underlines the importance of restoring and stabilising the riverbed in the goldmine rehabilitation process.

title: Soil carbon and nitrogen dynamics during the thermokarst lake succession under climate change on the Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Yuanhong Deng, Xiaoyan Li, Zhigang Wang, Shaojie Zhao, Fangzhong Shi
abstract: Thermokarst lakes (TLs) induced by permafrost thaw can disturb soil carbon and nitrogen cycling, creating positive feedbacks to climate warming. However, active-layer soil organic carbon (SOC) and total nitrogen (TN) dynamics across TL succession stages, as well as relative contributions of factors across spatial scales, remain unknown on the Tibetan Plateau (TP). For the first time, we investigated the expanding, stable, drying, and drained TLs on the TP, each with distinct microfeatures. We found that these TLs predominantly caused SOC and TN losses, peaking at the drying and drained stages; this divergence from the carbon accumulation in the Arctic is possibly due to the TP’s warm-dry climate. At the landscape scale, microfeatures, sand, soil water (SW), pH, and aboveground biomass explained over 50% of the variance in SOC, TN, and C:N at most sites, among which the local SW effect shifted from positive at water-limited sites (likely via mitigating water stress) to negative at water-sufficient sites (likely by exacerbating erosion). Regionally, background factors (climate, grazing, soil, and vegetation properties) explained over twice the variance in carbon and nitrogen metrics compared to within-landscape factors, with the background SW exhibiting the strongest effect. Projections incorporating climate-driven cascading effects through SW and pH showed that while future trajectories varied by TL stage, historical TL-induced C and N losses were likely irreversible under SSP climate scenarios. Our study demonstrates the need to incorporate fine-scale thermokarst processes (i.e., microfeatures and key hydroclimatic drivers) into Earth System Models to constrain uncertainty in projecting permafrost carbon-climate feedbacks.

title: Probabilistic prediction of maximum scour depth downstream of sluices and culverts using a tabular foundation model
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Duc-Hau Le
abstract: Accurate prediction of maximum scour depth downstream of hydraulic structures is essential for safe design and risk-informed assessment. Traditional empirical and machine-learning approaches typically provide deterministic predictions and often require extensive task-specific tuning, limiting their robustness under data-scarce conditions. This study investigates the application of TabPFN (Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network), a pre-trained foundation model for tabular data, for probabilistic prediction of scour depth downstream of culverts and sluice gates. Experimental datasets compiled from multiple laboratory studies are analyzed using a 4-fold cross-validation framework, and TabPFN is benchmarked against Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost models under an out-of-the-box setting. Results show that TabPFN achieves competitive or superior predictive performance with improved stability across folds. Beyond point predictions, the model provides full predictive distributions, enabling uncertainty quantification through prediction interval metrics, including Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP) and Mean Prediction Interval Width (MPIW). The results indicate well-calibrated and informative uncertainty estimates. Furthermore, the probabilistic outputs allow estimation of exceedance probabilities, supporting risk-informed and reliability-based design. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) confirm that the model captures physically meaningful relationships, with the densimetric Froude number (Fd ) identified as the dominant controlling factor. The findings demonstrate the potential of foundation models to deliver accurate, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware predictions for hydraulic engineering applications.

title: Co-metabolic-like effects induced by eutrophication-intensified cyanobacterial blooms enhanced sediment carbon emissions in shallow lakes
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Yu Peng, Weizheng Xie, Yaoqing Peng, Chuanqiao Zhou, Huazu Liu, Qiu Jin, Yiwen Zhou, Tsuyoshi Kinouchi, Hideyuki Doi, Xiaoguang Xu
abstract: Eutrophication‐intensified cyanobacterial blooms are increasingly recognized as significant contributors to carbon emissions from shallow lakes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we combined basin-scale field surveys, satellite-derived floating algae index (FAI), and microcosm incubations to evaluate the effects of cyanobacterial blooms on carbon emissions and sediment carbon loss in seven shallow lakes of the middle and lower Yangtze River Basin. FAI-based analyses showed severe and spatially extensive cyanobacterial blooms, with maximum bloom coverage reaching approximately 68.8% of the lake area in Taihu and nearly complete coverage in Dianshan, while bloom intensity correlated positively with trophic level. Field observations revealed that hypereutrophic lakes with higher total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), and organic carbon (OC) concentrations in the overlying water and sediments exhibited strongly elevated CH4 and CO2 fluxes; specifically, CH4 emissions in Taihu (248.6 μg·m−2·min−1) exceeded those in the mesotrophic Lake Caizi (7.1 μg·m−2·min−1) by over an order of magnitude. Furthermore, microcosm experiments demonstrated that cyanobacterial-derived labile carbon enhances the decomposition of macrophyte detritus via co-metabolic-like effect interactions: mixed cyanobacteria–plant treatments resulted in up to approximately 100% and 125% increases in CH4 and CO2 production, respectively, while sediment TOC loss exceeded theoretical expectations. These findings highlight that bloom-driven co-metabolic-like effect is a critical mechanism for amplifying carbon emissions and destabilizing sediment carbon pools in eutrophic lakes, highlighting the necessity of incorporating bloom dynamics and multi-source carbon interactions into regional and global lake carbon budgets.

title: Redox front delineation framework from self-potential data for characterizing groundwater contaminant plumes
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Jing Xie, Qinghua Huang, Yi-an Cui, Pu Wang, Lijuan Zhang, Hang Chen
abstract: Groundwater contamination from landfill leachate and hydrocarbon spills poses significant risks to water resources and public health. Conventional borehole-based monitoring methods provide accurate concentration data but are limited by sparse spatial coverage and an invasive nature. In contrast, self-potential (SP) surveys, as a non-invasive geophysical alternative, are particularly effective in detecting contaminant plumes through natural electric field variations. However, interpreting SP signals remains challenging due to overlapping electricity generation mechanisms in complex subsurface environments. This study develops an integrated redox front delineation framework combining advanced signal processing and imaging techniques to improve contaminant plume delineation. The framework consists of principal component analysis for source signal estimation, non-negative matrix factorization for target signal extraction, simulated annealing for SP amplitude and polarity recovery, and gradient-based inversion for SP source reconstruction. Laboratory experiments were conducted to validate the framework using two common SP signals in contaminated sites: microbial-mediated redox potential and fluid-related streaming potential. Results showed the framework significantly improved target signal extraction, with correlation coefficients increasing from 0.58 (microbial-related SP vs. mixed SP) to 0.85 (microbial-related SP vs. separated redox-type SP). The framework was then applied to field data from a municipal landfill, where the separated redox-related SP signals enabled more precise identification of contaminant plume boundaries compared to unprocessed data. This study provides a practical tool for the non-invasive characterization of contaminant plumes and the optimization of remediation strategies, advancing the deep cross-disciplinary application of geophysics, hydrogeophysics, and groundwater hydrology.

title: How uncertain are multi-source precipitation products in characterizing extreme precipitation?
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 677, Part B Author(s): Yixuan Wang, Aizhong Ye, Lingyun Wu
abstract: Given the increasing risks of extreme precipitation and the growing number of available precipitation products, it is necessary to comprehensively quantify uncertainties in how these products characterize extreme precipitation. This study uses 24 precipitation products across six categories over seven climatic zones in China to quantify uncertainty in the characterization of extreme precipitation and to identify consistent patterns in daily variability, annual trends, total amounts, event detection, and spatiotemporal displacement errors. The results show that: (1) Products show regional dependence across most evaluation dimensions, with larger discrepancies over the Tibetan Plateau and arid regions and higher consistency in humid regions, except for spatial displacement errors. (2) Detection errors are mainly from minor spatiotemporal misalignment rather than complete misses. Within acceptable spatiotemporal tolerance windows, for hit events with non-zero displacement, the non-zero typical mean absolute time offset across products ranges from about 1.1 to 1.3 days, and the non-zero typical mean spatial displacement is about 14.6 to 16.4 km. The systematic bias in extreme precipitation amounts for hit events is not pronounced. (3) Most products show broadly consistent relative error characteristics across regions: products with larger median spatial displacement and wider spread in one region often show similar patterns elsewhere. Temporal offsets show similar but weaker consistency, especially over the Tibetan Plateau and arid Northwest China. (4) The relative uncertainty characteristics of individual products within the 24-product ensemble differ across evaluation dimensions. These findings can support the assessment and interpretation of extreme precipitation, but their applicability is constrained by the selected reference dataset, daily 0.1° evaluation scale, and the many-to-one event-matching framework, which is designed to assess neighborhood detectability rather than strict event identity.

title: Experimental investigation on energy mechanical evolution and damage model of red limestone subjected to high-temperature water cooling cycling
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Haopeng Jiang, Hui Wang, Fengrui Zhang, Wei Yin
abstract: In geothermal development and high-temperature rock engineering, sedimentary geothermal surrounding rocks are prone to mechanical deterioration and damage accumulation under long-term high temperature effects, cold water recharge, and thermal-water circulation disturbances. In this study, red limestone collected from Ya’an, Sichuan Province, was investigated through a series of triaxial compression tests after exposure to different temperatures (200 °C, 400 °C, 600 °C, and 800 °C) and varying numbers of water-quenching cycles (0, 5, and 10). The degradation of the physical and mechanical properties of the limestone was systematically evaluated, and its energy evolution characteristics, including energy input, storage, dissipation, and release, were analyzed within the framework of energy dissipation theory. The results show that both the peak strength and elastic modulus of the red limestone decrease noticeably with increasing temperature and quenching cycles. The repeated action of thermal stress and rapid cooling promotes crack initiation and propagation between mineral grains, increases porosity, and leads to pronounced deterioration of the internal microstructure. In terms of energy behavior, the progressive accumulation of damage weakens the rock energy storage capacity and significantly raises the proportion of dissipated energy. Based on the experimental results, a statistical damage constitutive model incorporating a modified energy dissipation function was established. The validation results indicate that the proposed model can effectively characterize the nonlinear deformation behavior and strength response of red limestone after high-temperature water-cooling treatment. These findings provide an important theoretical basis for the efficient development of geothermal resources and the stability evaluation of high-temperature rock engineering.

title: Quantifying geothermal heat loss at the Dayoukeng crater using UAV thermal imaging and comparison with Landsat-derived estimates
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Hai-Po Chan, Yu-Chang Chan, Cheng-Wei Sun
abstract: This study quantifies geothermal radiative heat flux (RHF) and geothermal radiative heat loss (RHL) at the Dayoukeng (DYK) crater of Tatun Volcanic Group (TVG) in Taiwanusing both UAV thermal imaging and Landsat thermal infrared data. A dawn UAV survey minimized solar effects, acquiring 782 thermal images at 13 cm resolution. Land surface temperatures from both datasets were used to estimate RHF accounting for surface emissivity, atmospheric transmittance, and ambient temperature. Both datasets consistently delineate geothermal anomalies, while UAV imagery uniquely resolves fine-scale thermal heterogeneity. Maximum temperatures reach 84.4 °C in UAV data and 44.4 °C in Landsat, corresponding to peak RHF values of 214 and 62.6 Wm⁻², respectively. Despite differences in spatial resolution and peak values, geothermal heat loss estimates are comparable, with RHL of 210 MW derived from UAV data and 217 MW from Landsat observations, and are of similar order of magnitude to previous geochemical estimates based on the volumetric method. These results demonstrate that satellite thermal imagery provides an efficient tool for regional geothermal heat loss assessment, whereas UAV thermal imaging offers substantially enhanced detail on localized heat flux variability. This study presents the first UAV-based geothermal heat loss assessment at DYK within the Tatun Volcanic Group, northern Taiwan, and highlights the complementary strengths of UAV and satellite thermal observations for geothermal exploration and volcanic monitoring.

title: Limited heat connectivity across the Northeastern Segment of the Tanlu Fault, China: Implications for low–temperature geothermal systems
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jingyu Lin, Xuelian Huang, Shuai Wang, Shihua Qi, Xu Wang
abstract: The northeastern segment of the Tanlu Fault (NTLF) hosts predominantly low–temperature geothermal systems, contrasting with the high–temperature resources in the central and southern segments. To elucidate the factors controlling the low–temperature characteristics in the NTLF, we combined geochemical and isotopic analyses of geothermal and cold groundwater with numerical simulations. The results indicate that the geothermal waters are primarily recharged through meteoric water infiltration, with reservoir temperatures ranging from 60 °C to 110 °C and circulation depths extending from 1539 to 2972 m. Hydrogeochemical and isotopic evidence suggests prolonged water–rock interaction, relatively slow groundwater renewal, and limited contribution from high–temperature magmatic or deep hydrothermal fluids. Numerical simulations show that, under limited effective fault permeability, upward heat transfer from deeper thermal domains to shallow and intermediate reservoirs remains weak, and the temperature field is mainly controlled by conductive heat transfer. Sensitivity analyses further support that fault permeability strongly influences the efficiency of upward heat transfer. This study highlights that the geothermal significance of major fault zones depends not only on their structural scale, but also on effective fault connectivity that enables upward heat transfer.

title: Distribution characteristics and controlling factors of the thermal field and geothermal resource potential on the southern margin of the Junggar basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Junji Chen, Yingchun Wang, Haozhu Zhang, Yi Wang, Pengfei Chen, Guangzheng Jiang, Jie Hu
abstract: The existing heat flow measurement points in the southern margin of the Junggar Basin are unevenly distributed, with notable gaps in certain areas, resulting in insufficient spatial constraints on the regional geothermal field. Meanwhile, the deep temperature distribution remains poorly characterized and the genesis of geothermal systems has not yet to be fully elucidated. To address these issues, static well temperature data from 16 boreholes were collected and integrated with previously published rock thermophysical parameters to obtain 7 new high-quality terrestrial heat flow values, increasing the total number of measurement points from 31 to 38 and effectively filling the gaps in heat flow coverage. Building on these results, one-dimensional steady-state heat conduction equations were applied to calculate and analyze the planar distribution of the geothermal field at depths shallower than 2000 m, and a comprehensive assessment of geothermal resource potential was conducted in conjunction with regional geological data. The results show that the geothermal gradient ranges from 11.4 to 22.4 °C/km, with a mean of 17.8 ± 2.3 °C/km, and the terrestrial heat flow ranges from 23.4 to 44.5 mW/m², with a mean of 36.2 ± 4.7 mW/m². At burial depths of 500–2000 m, localized high-temperature thermal anomalies are identified in the Sikeshu Depression, the central Qigu Fault-Fold Belt, and the central Huomatu Anticline Belt, which are interpreted as local thermal anomaly zones on the southern margin of the Junggar Basin. The overall low heat flow background is primarily attributed to the combined effects of groundwater circulation, basement relief, structural configuration, and sedimentation rate. The total geothermal resources are estimated at 3823.6 × 10¹⁸ J, equivalent to 123.8 billion tons of standard coal; the Jurassic system contains the most abundant resources at 1066.1 × 10¹⁸ J, while the Quaternary and Neogene reservoirs have the least at 44.8 × 10¹⁸ J. The new heat flow data are consistent with previously published results, together corroborating the low geothermal background of the southern Junggar Basin. These findings provide an important reference for understanding the present-day geothermal field and for geothermal resource exploration and development in the study area.

title: Thermal conductivity evaluation using an integrated method: An example from the Horn River Basin, Canada
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Kezhen Hu, Wanju Yuan, Xiaojun Liu, Stephen E. Grasby, Zhuoheng Chen
abstract: The Horn River Basin in northeastern British Columbia, Canada, hosts significant unconventional shale-gas resources and geothermal potential within the Devonian Horn River Group (HRG). The organic-rich HRG shale is highly heterogeneous due to complex mineralogy and matrix variability across the basin, posing challenges for accurate thermal conductivity (TC) prediction. This study presents an integrated approach to evaluate spatial TC variability by combining comprehensive petrophysical characterization with two-phase mixing models: the Voigt–Reuss–Hill (VRH) average approach and the geometric mean (GM) method. Machine learning techniques were applied to extensive mineralogical data to predict mineral compositions from well logs, while total organic carbon (TOC), porosity, and fluid saturation were quantified through core–log calibrations and statistical analysis. TC profiles were then calculated using the VRH and GM models, incorporating calculated component volumes and mineral TC values adjusted for in situ temperature and pressure conditions. Both measured and modeled results indicate that TC in the low-porosity shale is predominantly controlled by mineralogy/lithology, increasing with quartz and carbonate content and decreasing with higher clay volume. Notably, the VRH approach performs better for lower TC values (<2.5 W/m·K) associated with higher clay and lower quartz and carbonate contents, whereas the GM method is more accurate at higher TC values (≥2.5 W/m·K), corresponding to lower clay and higher quartz and carbonate contents. Given the heterogeneous mineralogy and high TOC content of the HRG shale, integrating both models effectively captures the full range of TC variability and enhances predictive accuracy.

title: Integrated geothermometry for mixed-fluid carbonate geothermal systems under structural and hydrochemical constraints: Insights from the Yichuan Basin, central China
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Rudan Zheng, Gaoli Zhao, Jianhua Ping, Wei Leng, Joshua Mahwa, Jichang Zhao, Chengding Huo, Jiaqi Liu
abstract: Reliable characterization of reservoir temperature is an important step in geothermal resource evaluation, engineering design, and long-term utilization in sustainable subsurface energy systems. In groundwater-dominated geothermal systems hosted by fractured–vuggy carbonate reservoirs, conventional geothermometers often yield a wide range of temperature estimates owing to the combined effects of shallow groundwater mixing, re-equilibration, and hydrochemical buffering. These uncertainties hinder the interpretation of subsurface thermal regimes and groundwater circulation processes. In this study, we integrated hydrochemical indicators and environmental isotopes from the Yichuan Basin to constrain the fluid sources, circulation pathways, and mixing processes in a fault-controlled carbonate geothermal system. Building on hydrochemical and isotopic constraints on recharge, circulation, and mixing, we applied a multi-index-weighted geothermometer (MIWG) within a structure- and mixing-informed framework to estimate the reservoir temperatures in the Yichuan Basin. The results indicate that geothermal fluid evolution is jointly controlled by deep water–rock interactions and variable shallow groundwater mixing. Compared with individual geothermometers, the MIWG reduces the influence of method-specific extremes and yields more internally consistent well-specific temperature estimates. The MIWG-derived temperatures ranged from 78 to 157 °C across the study area, with the principal geothermal upflow system most plausibly concentrated at 128–157 °C. This study outlines a structure-informed interpretive framework for integrated geothermometry in mixed-fluid carbonate geothermal systems, distinguishing the indicative reservoir temperature range from the mixing-biased apparent temperatures. The proposed framework may help reduce the uncertainty in reservoir temperature assessment in structurally complex carbonate geothermal systems.

title: Reactive viscous fluid fracturing of volcanic rocks: Chemical weakening offsets viscosity-induced pressure increase
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Eko Pramudyo, Nagi Obata, Luis Salalá, Jiajie Wang, Noriaki Watanabe
abstract: Hydraulic stimulation of volcanic reservoirs can be hindered by strong fluid infiltration into pores, vesicles, and microfractures, which suppresses pressure build-up and limits the formation of conductive fractures. Increasing fluid viscosity can reduce fluid loss, but typically at the cost of higher fracturing pressure. Here, we tested whether this viscosity–pressure trade-off can be mitigated by combining viscosity control with chemical weakening of the rock matrix. Triaxial fracturing experiments were conducted at 180 °C on volcanic rocks using water-like fluids, non-reactive viscous fluids, and reactive viscous fluids composed of the biodegradable chelating agent N,N-bis(carboxymethyl)- L -glutamic acid (GLDA) and the biopolymer scleroglucan. Water-like fluids showed strong matrix infiltration and were ineffective at generating large-aperture fractures. Increasing viscosity suppressed infiltration and promoted wider fractures, but increased fracturing pressure. When GLDA was added to the viscous fluid, fracture aperture and fracture-network complexity increased further, while fracturing pressure in the benchmark andesitic tuff experiments remained comparable to that during water injection despite the much higher fluid viscosity. The results are consistent with chemically induced weakening offsetting the pressure increase normally associated with viscous fluids. Additional experiments on andesitic lava and rhyolitic reservoir rock suggest that reactive viscous fluids can also propagate pre-existing fractures and promote branching in volcanic rocks with contrasting pore structures. These findings highlight the potential of reactive viscous fluid fracturing as a low-pressure stimulation strategy for geothermal reservoirs, with possible relevance to proppant-less reservoir stimulation.

title: Potential assessment of critical raw materials from European geothermal fluids
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Laura Spitzmüller, Andrea Flores Salinas, Valentin Goldberg, Jens C. Grimmer, Rafael Villablanca-Ahues, Fabian Nitschke
abstract: The energy transition is accompanied by a growing demand for raw materials. The EU Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA) foresees at least 10% of raw material supply covered by domestic sources. Geothermal fluids have the potential to contribute significantly achieving this target. Beyond the well-known and extensively studied lithium resources in European geothermal fluids, additional potential for other elements exists. We assess the potential of 64 elements in geothermal fluids that are defined as critical and strategic raw materials or raw materials in general under the CRMA. This assessment is based on >4000 geothermal fluid analyses across Europe. In summary, 13 of the 64 assessed elements are identified to provide the largest potential based on (a) their concentrations in geothermal fluids, (b) their ability to contribute to domestic supply and reduce supply-chain risks, (c) their hypothetical market value, and (d) their geostrategic importance. These elements are Li, B, Mg, Si, Mn, Ge, As, Rb, Sr, Cs and Pb with high reliability and Sc and Pd with low reliability. At the lower end of the spectrum are nine elements with the lowermost potentials (Se, Zr, Nb, In, Sn, Te, Ta, Re, Bi) and the Rare Earth Elements. Our evaluation framework simultaneously considers abundance and availability, economic potential and geostrategic and environmental aspects, thereby improving comparability across elements. Having identified these 13 promising candidates, future research can be more effectively focused on detailed resource assessments and the development of targeted extraction strategies.

title: Sustainable cementitious blends incorporating rice husk ash and silica flour for geothermal well applications
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Eduardo Lins, Rafael Ventura, Fabio Pereira, Rodrigo Santiago, Antonio Martinelli, Julio Freitas
abstract: Geothermal wells expose cement sheaths to temperatures up to 300 °C, where Class G cement slurries lose mechanical strength, compromising well integrity and long-term zonal isolation. To address this challenge, this study investigated the use of rice husk ash (RHA), a sustainable silica-rich material, combined with silica flour (SF) as a partial replacement for cement in cementitious mixtures designed for geothermal well conditions. Six cementitious systems with a constant slurry density of 15 ppg and varying RHA and SF contents were prepared and cured at 300 °C and 2000 psi for 7, 14, and 28 days. The hardened specimens were characterized by uniaxial compressive strength (UCS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results showed that RHA significantly improved mechanical performance, increasing compressive strength by up to 4 times compared with the standard slurry. Higher RHA contents also reduced strength retrogression and promoted denser microstructures after prolonged curing. XRD analyses revealed the predominance of thermally stable phases, particularly tobermorite and xonotlite, which contributed to enhanced mechanical stability. These findings demonstrate that cement systems incorporating RHA and silica flour have significant potential to mitigate strength retrogression and enhance the high-temperature performance of geothermal well cementing applications.

title: Hydrogeochemical processes and thermal mechanisms of deep-buried uplift dolostone reservoirs in the North China Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Hankun Li, Jiexiang Li, Chuanxia Ruan, Zhilong Liu, Yun Chen, Feng Du
abstract: Deep-buried karst thermal reservoirs in large sedimentary basins, particularly those in the North China Basin, possess considerable exploitation and utilization potential. Within this basin, the Tianjin area constitutes a typical buried-uplift geothermal zone, where the deeply buried dolostone of the Wumishan Formation acts as the primary karst reservoir. Focusing on this reservoir, this study integrated hydrochemical analysis, environmental isotope analysis, and inverse hydrogeochemical modeling to investigate the circulation and evolution patterns of deep geothermal water, and to establish a conceptual model illustrating the heat accumulation and control mechanisms of the buried-uplift geothermal anomaly zone. The results indicate that the primary recharge source of the geothermal water is atmospheric precipitation in the northern Yanshan area, with no evidence of significant recharge from deeper high-temperature reservoir water. The geothermal fluids can be interpreted as leaching water derived from marine saline sedimentary rocks. Hydrochemically, the dominant water types are HCO3·Cl-Na and HCO3·SO4·Cl-Na. The hydrochemical composition is mainly controlled by host-rock leaching, carbonate precipitation, cation exchange, and sulfate reduction, with no evidence for significant mantle-derived inputs or magmatic degassing effects. Hydraulically, the Wumishan Formation exhibits favorable hydraulic connectivity across different tectonic units. The geothermal water generally flows from the northeast to the southwest, and locally migrates from the core of uplift zones toward both flanks. The degree of groundwater confinement increases progressively from the northeast to the southwest. The Shuangyao Uplift and Baitangkou Depression feature favorable groundwater flow conditions, whereas the Xiaohanzhuang Uplift serves as a groundwater stagnation zone. Collectively, the geothermal anomaly of the Tianjin buried uplift represents a “conduction-convection composite” geothermal system. Regional geothermal anomalies are primarily controlled by preferential conductive heat accumulation over basement uplifts and are locally influenced by groundwater convection within fault zones, while widespread intra-formational convection within the reservoir facilitates heat transfer and promotes reservoir temperature homogenization.

title: Field-validated thermodynamic assessment of hybrid gas-removal systems for geothermal power plants
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Suyanto, Triyogi Yuwono, Lina Agustina, Bambang Teguh Prasetyo, Budi Ismoyo
abstract: Non-condensable gas accumulation in geothermal condensers increases condenser pressure, raises turbine backpressure, and reduces steam expansion performance. Conventional steam jet ejector systems remove these gases but consume motive steam that would otherwise contribute to power generation. This study evaluates a hybrid gas-removal configuration combining a steam jet ejector and a liquid-ring vacuum pump using operational data from the Kamojang geothermal field, Indonesia. A steady-state thermodynamic model was developed in Engineering Equation Solver to integrate turbine expansion, condenser behaviour, gas-removal processes, cooling systems, and auxiliary power consumption into a unified mass and energy-balance framework. The model was validated against operational data from Kamojang Units 2–4, with deviations of <5% in the principal operating parameters. At a gross turbine output of 56 MW, the hybrid configuration reduced total steam demand from 398,520 to 392,760 kg/h, a reduction of 5760 kg/h (1.45%). The hybrid system required an additional 156.3 kW of liquid-ring vacuum pump power and produced a net output of 54,359 kW, compared with 54,513 kW for the conventional ejector system. Ejector outlet pressure was optimised using total power-penalty minimisation, with the minimum penalty occurring at approximately 0.33 bar abs. Parametric analysis showed lower specific steam consumption for the hybrid configuration at higher non-condensable gas concentration and condenser pressure. The hybrid configuration became economically favourable when steam cost exceeded USD 0.03614/kWh or non-condensable gas concentration exceeded 0.10185%. The results demonstrate the trade-off between reduced motive-steam consumption and increased auxiliary power demand in hybrid gas-removal systems.

title: Liquid nitrogen as a waterless fracturing fluid for enhanced geothermal systems: Mechanisms, challenges, and opportunities
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): C. Beddage, P.G. Ranjith, S.Q. Yang
abstract: Liquid nitrogen (LN₂) cryogenic fracturing has gained increasing attention as a waterless stimulation approach for Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS), offering a potential alternative to conventional hydraulic fracturing in high-temperature reservoirs. By inducing rapid thermal contraction, phase transition, and vapor pressurization, LN₂ can stimulate rock without the use of water or chemical additives, thereby reducing water demand and associated environmental constraints. This review summarizes recent advances (2024–2025) based on laboratory experiments, numerical modelling, and field experience from hydrocarbon reservoirs, noting that no full-scale geothermal LN₂ field trials have yet been reported. Laboratory studies show that LN₂ treatment can result in 13.6–76% reductions in compressive strength and up to 86% in tensile strength, three-to-five-fold increases in permeability, and up to 48% enhancement in fracture connectivity. Irreversible thermo-mechanical damage is consistently observed once reservoir temperatures exceed a critical transition window of 200–300 °C. Complementary thermo-hydro-mechanical damage models predict breakdown pressure reductions of 7.14–46.15%, in good agreement with experimental observations. These characteristics, lower fracture initiation pressures, increased fracture complexity, and substantial reduction or, in some cases, complete elimination of water use during fracture initiation, are particularly attractive for EGS development in arid and water restricted regions. Despite these advantages, important challenges remain, including cryogenic fluid handling, limited proppant transport capacity, uncertainties in long term fracture stability, and the absence of field scale geothermal validation. Future research should focus on pilot scale geothermal demonstrations, optimization of hybrid LN₂ assisted stimulation strategies, and comprehensive techno-economic assessment. LN₂ cryogenic fracturing represents a high potential, though not yet field proven, stimulation pathway for next generation geothermal energy development.

title: Tracing the source and evolution of organic matter in geothermal environments
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Val Maverick Abecia, Andrea Vieth-Hillebrand, Sonia Salah, Ben Laenen, Simona Regenspurg, Valérie Cappuyns
abstract: Despite recent advances in molecular characterization of organic matter in geothermal fluids, its origin, transformation processes, and physicochemical properties remain poorly understood. It can be assumed that dissolved organic matter (DOM) originates from the geothermal reservoir rocks (natural organic matter, NOM) and from anthropogenic additives such as scaling and corrosion inhibitors (synthetic organic matter, Synthetic OM) mixed with the geothermal fluid during operation. In this study, Liquid Chromatography-Organic Carbon Detection (LC-OCD) was used to characterize NOM and Synthetic OM contributions to the geothermal brine. NOM leachability from reservoir rocks was investigated by batch leaching experiments using 3.5 mol L − 1 NaCl at 125 °C and 70 °C. Synthetic OM contribution was assessed by studying the thermal degradation of three inhibitor types (acrylates, phosphonates, and a commercial inhibitor mixture) diluted in 3.5 mol L − 1 NaCl, also at 125 °C and 70 °C. The results show that the leachable NOM fraction (3%–10%) is primarily composed of hydrophilic low molecular weight organics and macromolecules, with minor hydrophobic components. Synthetic organics from antiscalants and chemical inhibitors degrade under high temperature and salinity conditions, releasing diverse organic molecules. They can form organic precipitates that may clog filters in geothermal installations when an inappropriate inhibitor is selected, thereby impairing geothermal plant operations. Comparison with organic matter in natural geothermal brines reveals that their molecular weight distribution is the same as that of NOM and Synthetic OM, with low molecular weight organics predominating. Characterizing commercial inhibitor mixtures remains challenging due to undisclosed formulations, as well as analytical limitations. Although low resolution chromatographic methods provide valuable information on compositional characteristics of DOM and on molecular weight distribution, they do not allow an unequivocal distinction between NOM and Synthetic OM, justifying the need for high resolution chromatographic techniques and other complementary analytical methods.

title: Geochemical dynamics and predictive modeling of water-rock interaction during geothermal reinjection in coal mine gobs
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Yuanyuan Jiang, Xincheng Hu, Jiawen Cai, Guangping Huang, Zhaoyang Yu, Chengkai Fan, Shengqiang Yang
abstract: Geothermal reinjection in mine gobs is a promising method for geothermal energy exploration, but the heat mining efficiency can be reduced by the corrosion or scaling within pipelines caused by water-rock interaction. To elucidate the hidden mechanism, we conducted constant-temperature oscillation and water quality experiments and then established partial least squares (PLS) prediction models for water-rock interaction development prediction. The hydrochemical classification showed that the hydrochemical type shifted from 18-A to 21-A attributing to mineral dissolution, precipitation, and cation exchange during reinjection. The self-organizing mapping (SOM) and ion-ratio analysis revealed that there were three major ion sources: carbonate, evaporite, and silicate dissolutions. Additionally, rock pore structure and saturation index (SI) analysis illustrated that mineral precipitation was the leading water-rock interaction process to the decline of ion concentrations (i.e., Na⁺, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+, Cl-, SO4 2-, HCO3 -). Notably, Chlor-alkali index (CAI) analysis revealed that positive cation exchange was the key geochemical process, leading to the abundance of Na⁺ and the depletion of Ca²⁺and Mg²⁺. The mean square errors and determination coefficients of the established SI and CAI prediction models illustrated that the prediction results accorded well with the experiment results, providing a feasible method to predict the development of water-rock interaction during geothermal reinjection in gobs.

title: Hydraulic fracturing experimental study of high temperature granite with water and supercritical carbon dioxide
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Zheng Jiang, Biao Shu, Yongpeng Hu, John McLennan
abstract: Geothermal energy is a clean and renewable energy resource that can help reduce carbon emissions. Supercritical carbon dioxide (ScCO2) has been proposed as a substitute for water in hydraulic fracturing of deep geothermal reservoirs, due to its unique physical properties. Laboratory hydraulic fracturing experiments using water and ScCO2 were conducted to compare their fracturing performance. The experiments were carried out at temperatures of 50, 150, and 250 °C, and the confining pressures of 5, 10, and 15 MPa, respectively. The results show the breakdown pressures of ScCO2 fracturing are about 15.0-48.6% lower than those of water fracturing. Analytical calculation of breakdown pressure shows that Hubbert and Willis model provides a reasonable estimate for water fracturing with an average percentage error of 13.3%, while modified Haimson and Fairhurst model, which considered pore pressure distribution, works better for ScCO2 fracturing with an average percentage error of 6.8%. The fractures generated by ScCO2 fracturing predominantly propagate along mineral grain boundaries, but those generated by water fracturing typically cut directly through mineral grains. In addition to a dominant fracture, ScCO2 fracturing generated an average of 6 secondary fractures, while water fracturing generated an average of only 1 secondary fracture. The number of secondary fractures in ScCO2 fracturing increases significantly with increasing temperature, from an average of 2 at 50 °C to 11 at 250 °C.
